I used to snicker at my husband for always wanting packs of nylon ties around. He'd toss in various sizes and lengths, and I never really knew why.

Well, now I get it.
As I have begun trying to prepare for various scenarios, as well as get more organized, I see the value of these ties. I've used them to control loose cords, seal up some kinds of packages and even reenforced a small, rolling metal shelf.

Overall, very happy with these. I know you can get them cheaper in a store, but my mobility is limited, so online works just fine for me.

I know my husband always had cable ties all over the place. I used to wonder why. Now I know.

The cable ties are so useful for so many things! I have them in several sizes now. I use them to keep old cords wrapped up, to tie like items together, and most recently, to bolster a very shakey little wire shelf.

Our local store where I normally buy these has been out for nearly a year. While you pay a little bit more online, I'm still very glad I got them. No problems with these at all.

It is hard to have problems with zip ties, but I do have an issue with these. I had an entire bag of mystery cords that had entangled themselves like coat hangers do in dark closets. So, I sat myself down with the big bag, and a new plastic bin to bring some order to the chaos and bind up the cords. I had several sizes of zip ties with me to accomplish this task. The only black ties I had were these, so I know the issues I had were with these ties.

These are thinner than all the rest of my ties. Also, my others were made of nylon and were nice and strong. These black ties seemed to be more plastic than any nylon. They were a little harder to use, being a bit flimsy and much weaker than my other ties.

They did hold small cords together, but we're definitely cheaper and thinner. I would not buy these again.

These are super great to have on hand. You never know when you will have something unruly to contain, like extension cords.

I used to tease my husband for always buying zip ties, but now I get it. We even stabilized a shakey metal rolling cart with nylon zip ties!

Okay, I realize that everyone's definition of "easy to set up" comes from a different place. For me, I've worked around computers for over 25 years now, so pretty comfortable, BUT - I am more comfortable with software than hardware. So although this should not have been intimidating, it was a little bit. I formerly was using a Linksys router on our home network. It did a fine job, and was very easy to maintain. However, it didn't give much of a boost to the downstairs connections. The computer was always slow, and would drop the connection from time to time, and require a reboot to get the connection back.

This router is truly great looking. It is white, sleek and has nice blue lights. It sits vertically, rather than horizontally like my old one. I wasn't sure I'd like it, but I do. It comes with three screw-on antennas that can be pointed in any direction to boost your signal in that direction. The metal frame is very sturdy and would take a LOT of pressure to bend. I currently have mine on a separate little shelf because my current desk is too small.

There is only a quick set-up sheet included with this item. Ironically, if you need help, it tells you to go to the company's WEBSITE! Ha! So, if you can't get it to work, go ahead and get online. Yeah, No. But, if you are willing to disconnect and reset up a single-user home network using your old router, it could work! The sheet does give you very plain graphic instructions that tells you which item to plug in where, which many will find very helpful It came with a very short ethernet cord, so you either need to keep the router close to you or buy a longer cord. (The one I had was just purchased last year and was six feet long, so I was in good shape.)

Now, I couldn't get it to connect right away. The short troubleshooter on the insert says to reboot your modem, then to reboot the router. I did. Several times. The computer refused to acknowledge the new router! I was ready to just reconnect my Linksys when I decided to go against all logic and swap the ethernet and modem cords. For many years, computers and peripherals have been fairly color-coded to make it easier for non-tekkies to hook things up. In this case for the TP Link, the ethernet ports (there are four) are yellow and the modem port is blue. I even had previously bought color-coded wires so I didn't accidentally pull the wrong one. After 45 minutes of not being able to connect, I take another look at the back. Everything is in the right spot. But, since I wasn't connecting anyway, I decided to swap out the modem cord and ethernet cord, plugging yellow into the blue slot and the blue cord into the yellow slot. Totally backwards. As you might guess, it took off immediately! So apparently, our unit was either labeled backwards or connected backwards on the inside. Seriously strange. But as long as it works, I don't much care.

The default setting of this router is PUBLIC, so be sure to change your settings to PRIVATE NETWORK, if you don't want everyone in the neighborhood to try and tap into your network. Yes, they would need your password, but there are a lot of smart hackers out there, so you just never know. Better safe than sorry. There are default settings for the account name, network name (your SSID) and passwords, so you will need to change those as soon as you can. (If you forget to write them down, there is a reset button on the back to rol it back to the default passwords.) I also had to change the other settings to WPA2 for our area for the home network. No big deal, just different from before.

The TP Link C9 runs two parallel bands - 2.4Ghz, which is what most home routers use for regular internet access and browsing, and a 5.0 Ghz band, which is for streaming videos and movies. The nice thing about this router, is that if you name BOTH the 2.4 and the 5.0 the same name, it will AUTOMATICALLY switches to the strongest network for your use. I love that! The on/off switch is on the back of the router, so it won't easily get bumped. While my photos show the antennas straight up (we haven't had to move any of them to get a better reception), they rotate and bend towards whatever area you might need a little boost.

Has our reception improved? Yes! The downstairs computer now cruises like it was directly connected to a wired access point. The kids can watch movies and I can browse the net without anyone slowing down. The reception range is fabulous - we live in a multi-unit building, and could probably provide internet connection to all four units. It offers connection speeds of 1.3Gbps over the clearer 5GHz bandwidth and 600Mbps on the 2.4GHz bandwidth. We have not yet found a dead spot in our place - even outside picks up the signal.

In addition to the fabulous signal and great connection speeds, this router can also handle your USB 2.0 and 3.0 devices. There are ports on the side of the router, so you can easily transfer files, photos or data from an external drive to your own computer, or even hook up your printer to print wirelessly. (I haven't tried that yet, but the possibilities are there.)

It also offers a "tether" function for your smartphones. I have not used that, and won't be using that, but it would be great for parents who want to monitor network access/usage from work for their older kids. It is nice to know that option is there.

I am so very pleased with this router! I probably would not have looked at this brand, since I tend to stick with the equipment companies I've had previous success with, but I cannot state enough that this would be an asset to anyone's home network setup.

This is our second purchase of this case,
My daughter bought the blue case for her external hard drive back up.
The blue shade in the photo is very accurate. I would assume that the black
would also be fine. My monitor is very carefully callibrated, as I do some
graphics work. I haven't had anything so different on the color in the photo
as this one is in a long time. Go by the words in this case! They show a pink
case, but the text says magenta. The text is closer to real color. The case I
received is a deep purple/pink color. Since it will be in a drawer protecting my
external drive, it isn't a big problem. However, if you are someone who wants
to color-coordinate all your electronics, just be aware that it isn't actually pink.

That being said, the case is nice enough. It zips shut, which is great.
Note that the edges of the case are harder, and would protect against
being smashed. However, if you plan to toss this into a crowded backpack
or briefcase, know that the middle part of this case is NOT hard and can
easily be pushed in.

All in all, this is a nice case and will store your hard drive well.

This is my daughter's third MP3 player.
She wanted to try this one, since she loved the look of the design.
We figured how bad can a player be, right?
After seeing hers, my son ordered the same player.

Well, they do play music - for a while.
They also play videos nicely, albeit very small and hard to see.

As of today, with neither one a year old yet, one has had be to be sent back
to Sansa for work (totally locked up and could not even be rebooted). They took a
month to send back a refurb, rather than the one my son sent in with his music on it.

My daughter's lasted a little longer, but does freeze up often.
However, the latest trick is that it has part of the sound going out.
She had purchased four pairs of various headphones trying to get the sound to stop
cutting out, thinking it was the headphone's problem. Nope - turns out, it is the
player. Don't know what is wrong, but one of the stereo sides cuts in and out endlessly.

She'll be shopping for a new one, but it won't be this model anymore.
They are just too cheaply made to last. The technology has been around for a long time now,
and it shouldn't be that hard to make a decent, affordable player.
However, it seems like it might just be too hard for Sansa.

My daughter has used this cooler for almost three years. Yes, it takes a lot of special handling
for it to last that long - it gets tucked back into a laptop case every night.

It is an acrylic base, but not a thick one. It will definitely hold your laptop, but it really needs
to be on a flat surface to work properly. The blue lights look really great. It isn't too noisy,
unless you tip it - then it sounds like something grinding.

My daughter kind of killed hers off from repeatedly using her laptop on an uneven surface.
It caused the fans to stall out or grind, and burned them out. Right now, the cooler only has
one of the three fans working, and doesn't really keep the laptop cool enough.

Top points for looks - the acrylic and the blue lights are great. The price is good for what it is.
Got an expensive laptop? Get a different cooler - look for one that blows heat instead of tries to suck
heat (via the fans) away from the laptop. Try a Belkin. Forget Targus unless you don't mind going deaf while
cruising the internet.

Would I buy it again? Well, I think it would be a great low-cost alternative for a NETbook.
For a laptop, it would really be better to get something that has a stronger air movement capacity.

here is my review of the polk audio psw10

low cost, easy to install, aesthetically pleasing(looks very nice), porting, made from composite material that will last a long time, auto shut off feature when not in use, very good sound quality, nice and crisp not "boomy" bass, very good owners manual and customer support/service from polk audio.

Cons:
Low wattage, no cables included, not down firing port and no low-frequency effect (LFE)support.

conclusion:

I actually had to turn it down because it was so loud when i was first was setting it up and testing it( I have worked with Jet engines that require double hearing protection for years). I don't know how loud some people watch their TVs or movies but, this is way more than loud enough.It shakes my house.

Whether or not you'll like this case depends to a large extent on two things: 1) how much of a klutz you are, and 2) how you use your iPad.

Here's where I fit into that picture: I'm not generally klutzy -- I can count on one hand the number of times I've dropped any of my portable electronics in the past 10 years. I use my iPad mostly when I travel and don't want to bring my laptop, and it stays in my bag unless I'm using it. Otherwise, I bring it out now and again for games or to read (I have the Kindle app installed, and it works great for that). For me, this Otterbox case is probably a case of "overkill": perhaps a little more case than I really need.

The basics:
This is a multi-part case: the two-piece inner plastic "shell" with a clear window over the screen, the outer silicone "slipcover" that hugs the back and sides of the plastic shell, and another hard plastic snap-on outer "cover" that includes a pop-up stand, that snaps onto the back of the silicone cover.

The good:
This will definitely protect your iPad Pro 9.7. The thing is built like body armor -- solid, form-fitting, not too difficult to install. The colors "damson purple" and "hibiscus pink" aren't too garish, either, and match the photos on the page here.

The concern(s): The only screen protection is the thin plastic "screen protector" -- that's all. I'm a little concerned about how protective it would be in an accident. It would have been really nice if they had designed the outer cover/stand to snap onto the FRONT of the case. I've tried it a few times, and it doesn't work. The corner "clips" get caught in the silicone slipcover so that it can't snap securely. It only fits securely onto the BACK of the case. Pity.

Also, it's VERY heavy. I realize that you don't get this level of protection without adding weight, so that's a trade-off that you either choose to live with or not.

Soooo ... bottom line: if you have klutzy tendencies, if you're looking for 5-star protection for your iPad Pro and you're willing to live with added weight, this might be a super option. If you're more like me -- light user, not of the klutzy persuasion -- this might a little more protection than you really need. For me, it rates 3 stars: "It's OK."

I've been using a Keurig machine for several years -- I currently own 2 of them. But I've always had an ethical issue with all the little plastic cups that get tossed into the environment. To that end, I've tried and used several different varieties of reusable K-cups, and had finally settled on the Ekobrew cups.

I was offered an opportunity to try this set, and decided to do a side-by-side comparison. The results were interesting. These Brewooze cups perform just as good as the more expensive Ekobrew cups.

I tried several different coffees and several different grinds. As with all reusable cups, you have to be careful how fine/coarse the grind is. Too coarse, and you get weaker coffee; too fine, and you get either overflow and/or sludge. I found that a medium-fine grind worked best for both cup brands. This way, I get the right strength and almost no powdery sludge in the bottom of the cup. One advantage of the Brewooze over the Ekobrew: I was able to use LESS coffee in the cup to get the right brew strength. With the Ekobrew, I needed to fill the cup; with the Brewooze, I filled it about 2/3 full to get the same flavor/strength.

As with all reusable K-cups, you need to take care when you seal them prior to use. These are no trouble to seal correctly -- you can easily see if there are gaps and do an extra "squeeze." Inserting them into the machine takes a bit of attention, too -- otherwise, you can pierce the cup. There are arrows on the lid that show which direction, so that shouldn't be a problem.

This set comes with 20 paper filters plus a replacement charcoal filter for the Keurig filter wand. I didn't see much advantage to the paper filters except possibly ease of cleaning. The coffee was weaker, and using a finer grind didn't seem to help. And it still resulted in some grinds getting "around" the paper filter and onto the mesh, so I still had to clean the cup. It's not a big deal, really -- the cups are easy to rinse clean after use. So I won't be using the paper filters, but you may find them useful.

I'm a little surprised at how nicely these performed, given the price. You get 3 cups (brown, medium tan, and light tan color -- the photo makes them look orange, but they're more of a tan/brown), so if you want to assign a color to different family members, there you go. Since I usually brew 2 cups into a large mug, I just fill 2 of them with the same coffee and run them one after the other in the morning.

kI have to say I was impressed. I didn't expect these to perform as well as they did. I've been using these for about 4 days, and after the initial side-by-side test (when I brewed about 12 cups total), I've been brewing 2-3 cups every morning, rotating them, cleaning after each use, and so far, no signs of any wear problems. If I notice a serious issue, I'll update this review.

Sample supplied for review; opinions expressed are based on my personal experience with this product.

I'm not the most skilled at applying these sticky screen protectors. I usually end up with bubbles, so I rip it off, and start over with a new one. Obviously, I migrate toward the lower-priced ones since I usually end up wasting at least one in a 3-pack.

I'm happy to report I got the first one of these installed without a single bubble. Either I'm getting better at this, or there's something different about these protectors. The process is a bit different from others I've used, but the instructions are clear and application was easy.

Can't speak to the durability of these as I've had mine installed for just 10 days or so, but for inexpensive basic screen protectors for your iPhone 5 series, you can't do any better than these. Highly recommended!

I've been using this cable daily for over a week, and I have to say I'm impressed so far.

It's a solid, sturdy cable -- "thicker" than the original, not quite as flexible, but that doesn't bother me. The USB and lightning plugs are securely attached, and it doesn't look like there will be any problems with the cord cover fracturing at either point (I've had that problem with other cables, including the original one that came with an earlier iPhone). The plugs seat securely into my charger and iPhone 5S, too. I have a Case Logic rubber case [[ASIN:B00JMPXGOQ Case Logic CLIPH5-3203 iPhone 5/5s 2-piece Hand Grip - White/Gray]] on my iPhone, and the cord fits just fine.

The cord is 10' long -- that's longer than any of my other cords, and will come in handy for those times when I need to recharge from a plug that's not nearby. This is NOT a "small" cord -- it's going to take up some space while traveling, but to me, it's worth it.

So far, I have noticed no issues at all. It plays nicely with my iPhone, with no hiccups or problems. I'll be traveling with it soon, and will update this review if I notice any issues at all. Otherwise, so far, I'm impressed. I received a sample for review purposes, with no assurance of a positive review. My opinion is based solely on my experience with the product.

I got this to store the back-up of my external hard drive, and it does that job very well. I have a key chain on which I store a number of flash drives for various purposes that I leave hanging on a hook in my office, so it doesn't get a lot of abuse. So far, I've noticed no problems with quality -- it's VERY small, and fits VERY snugly into the USB port on my laptop, but once I get it right-side up, it's easy to insert and retrieve.

Speed is adequate for my needs. Very happy with this so far. If that changes, I'll edit this review.

OK, let's get this straight at the beginning: I'm not an audio expert. I don't work in the industry, I haven't studied this stuff, etc. But I DO know what sounds good especially when it comes to classical music recordings. I've been involved in classical music my whole life, I've played and sung with orchestras, so I know how things should sound.

Bottom line: this unit produces very good quality sound over the range of dynamics and timbres that come with a variety of classical music. I have a few recordings that I use as "tests": Carmina Burana (the opening "O Fortuna" section); Bach "Magnificat"; Stravinsky "Firebird"; Mozart piano sonatas; Beethoven String Quartets; and various choral works (Eric Whitacre, Brahms, etc.). I got none of the tinny sound that sometimes happens with piano works; the softer sections of the Eric Whitacre choral works were clear and precise; the range of dynamics in the opening O Fortuna of "Carmina Burana" was crystal clear with no distortion. Really, this outperformed my expectations.

The unit is smaller than I expected, which is a good thing, since I intend to take it along when I travel. It's attractive (I got the orange color), and has a nice "feel" to it. The controls are easy to manipulate on the top of the unit, and I really like the ability to take phone calls via the unit (it has a built-in microphone).

Overall, I'm very pleased with this purchase. I paid less than forty dollars for mine, and at that price, I consider it a super deal. I've had it only for a couple of weeks, so if there are issues with durability, I'll update this review. For now, it's definitely worth 5 stars.

Got this to use while traveling, when a longer cable comes in handy. I've been using it daily for two weeks, and so far, no problems. I use the [[ASIN:B00ESJGILE AmazonBasics  Case for iPhone 5S & iPhone 5 - White / Grey]], and it fits just fine. Absolutely no issues or complaints; would definitely purchase again.

I got this to use as a back-up cable for my iPad 2 when I travel. I've used it in two trips so far, and it's holding up just fine.

Everything fits snugly, nothing looks like it's about ready to fall apart, and it performs just like the original Apple cable. The 4-foot length is nice, too.

Very happy with this, and would purchase again.

I did a LOT of research before purchasing this little speaker. My needs were pretty simple: I wanted a wireless speaker that could connect with either my iPhone or iPad to use on the nightstand. I like to play music before I go to sleep, so it needed to be small, but have great sound.

Based on the reviews here, I finally decided on this one, and I'm happy to say it's PERFECT!

It charged quickly connected to my MacBook Pro -- about 2 hrs, maybe a little less. Turned it on, turned on the iPhone, went to the "Settings" on the phone, found Bluetooth, and there was the JAM XT. Selected it, and voila! they paired. Entire set-up took about 10 seconds.

I listen to a lot of classical music, so my first "test" was the Brahms "A German Requiem" -- lots of highs, lows, soft, loud, etc. Strings, voices, woodwinds, brass -- it's all in there. I listened carefully for distortion -- everything was set on "medium" volume -- and I'm happy to say I heard NO distortion at all. Everything sounded great -- nearly as good as my Bose system, but without the bass resonance.

OK, so I haven't had this very long (about a week), so its durability remains to be seen. But I'm impressed with the quality and style of this. If I notice any issues, I'll update this review.

Meanwhile, I can now fall asleep to great sounding music from a small-footprint speaker. And that's exactly what I wanted.

I have an Epson LW-300, and this tape is specifically designed for use with the Epson LabelWorks series. The 1/2" size is perfect for my needs, and the white with black print works great.

The BEST thing this has going for it is the split backing. I can print a label, then peel off the upper half of the backing, leaving the lower half in place. This way, I can easily get proper placement before peeling off the lower half of the backing and making the placement more permanent.

Very happy with this -- definitely will continue using it for all my labeling needs.

So far, so good -- this is a very nicely made stylus that works perfectly with my iPad. I really like the "slim" profile, especially the smaller tip that allows for greater precision. I'm prone to losing my styluses (styli?), so having the little gizmo that fits into the earphone jack to tether the stylus to the tablet is a very good thing.

I'm recommending this one to my friends who are new to tablets. The price is good and the quality is better than expected.

I got this to replace the original cable that came with my iPhone 3GS which had more or less disintegrated (both ends were coming loose).

So far, it's working just fine. I use it every day or so to recharge the battery, and I've used it to sync my iPhone with my Mac. I like that it's 6' long, which gives me a little more play. It seems sturdy enough, too.

I don't go through a lot of CDs, but so far, I've burned maybe 20 or so, and I've not had a single failure. I use CDs mostly to make copies of mp3s of my own choral compositions (done in Finale) to help my singers learn their parts easier. Playback has been perfect on each disk -- at least, my singers have had no complaints at all.

Someone else mentioned the amount of surface space available for adding label info on the disk -- this has been really helpful for me. On many brands, the brand logo and extras are printed in multiple colors (or black) on the surface, and take up a huge amount of real estate. The printed Verbatim logo/etc. on this disk is silver on silver -- relatively plain -- so you can write all over it easily. And I do.

Amazon's price is very good, too. Good product, good price, serves a specific purpose -- for casual use, I'd say these are an excellent choice.

I got this to "expand" my MacBook Pro laptop. The MacBook Pro has only two USB connections, one on each side, and I usually have my printer and midi keyboard connected. I often found myself having to unplug something so I could upload photos or sync my iPhone.

This little Saitek Mini UFO Hub solved the problem. I can plug it into one of the two USB outlets on the laptop, and immediately I have four new usable connections available. This lets me keep connected everything that I use regularly. It doesn't take up much room, either.

This is a great little problem solver.

I am amazed at how good these speakers are for the size. I've been using them with my iPod nano as well as my laptop, and they're really quite good. Others have mentioned the lack of bass, and I agree -- it could use a little more "oomph" on the low end. But it's not that bad, really -- and the overall sound is really excellent.

This little unit is truly portable, with its own little drawstring bag. I've been able to fit everything -- the power cord, the unit, and the device cord -- into the bag. It's a tight fit, but it works.

I'm very please with the On Tour speakers -- definitely recommend them if you need something portable to provide more/better sound than your internal laptop speakers or something to connect to an MP3 player. Look for them on sale (I got mine via a Goldbox special).

If you can get only one add-on for your digital camera, let it be this one.
I took my Kodak digital camera decked out with this 128MB CompactFlash card on a 6-week road trip. I used the "middle" quality setting for the pictures, and managed to take over 130 photos (the equivalent of 5-6 24-shot rolls of film), filling not anywhere close to half the card (at that setting, the card will store over 300 photos)!
I'm not a digital photography technoid by any stretch of the imagination -- I just like capturing memories of the places I go and the things I see. Having the extra memory afforded by this little card meant that I could relax and not worry about running out of space for all my photos.
Transferring the photos to my laptop was a piece of cake, and took very little time -- partially a function of the card.
I highly recommend this as the *first* accessory/upgrade you purchase for your camera!

I'm just an amateur when it comes to photography. All I really want is an easy-to-use point-and-shoot camera that I can take on vacations to snap shots of places I find interesting, to use around the house to take photos of valuables for insurance purposes, etc. In other words, my expectations are pretty minimal.
That said, I'm extremely happy with the Kodak DC3400. This is my second Kodak digital (my first was a DC240), so obviously I'm pleased with the Kodak product line.
After unpacking the DC3400, I spent about 10 minutes getting it set up, and proceeded to take a few pictures. Another 10 minutes or so, and I had the photo software loaded on my laptop. Connect the USB cable, and I was able to load the photos onto the laptop immediately. The camera shows up as an icon, like a disk drive, which you can double-click to open and transfer the pictures to a folder on your hard drive -- piece of cake!
The quality of the pictures is amazing. I use the Ofoto service, and had some prints of some of my digital photos sent to my mother. According to her, you could not tell the difference between the digital images and those taken with a 35mm film camera. The colors were vivid, the images sharp -- just what you'd expect from the Kodak name.
I'll agree with most everyone else and say that batteries might be the only downside to this camera. It's definitely worth the investment to get the Kodak NiMh rechargables and the charger. The ONLY time I use NiCads is when I'm my NiMh set is in the recharger, and I need to snap a few pictures.
For the money, I don't think you can top this camera in terms of features, quality, and ease of use.

The packaging and marketing hooked me in, where I was compelled to try this.
I have a small table next to my recliner. This stand/platform is good as a riser for the table to increase its height. The stand is super easy & fast to get the legs on. The quality is good.

The original Sony remote control that came with the TV is way too big. It is so long. Unnecessarily long, with a lot of empty space. This RMF-TX900U is the perfect size. It feels solid. It lights up automatically if you pick it up in a dark room. And it takes up way less space than the original remote control.

There is a great feature of this TV, as it has the Google Voice Assistant built in. You can either access the Voice Assistant by holding the microphone button down on the remote control, where the remote's mic sends your command to the TV, or by simply (and more conveniently) speaking out loud, saying the Google Wake Words, and then the TV's internal microphone hears you and Google responds. You can control a lot of features just with your voice, without having to touch the remote control. This includes turning the TV off, or muting the sound, or lowering or raising the volume, etc.

However, on the TV I received, the internal microphone is dead. Or, it's some other hardware failure. Yes, the microphone switch is set to the ON position. Yes, the setting to allow my voice to control the TV is on. Yes, 2 separate Sony tech support reps accessed my TV via the Remote Access feature and went through everything. It was extensive. Yes, the TV has all the updates, and a factory reset was done. The TV's microphone will not respond at all to the Hey Google or OK Google command.

I deducted 2 stars because at this price, this 2022 Sony TV really should be 1080p instead of 720p, there really should be HDMI CEC (Sony calls this Bravia Sync), and because the remote control is way too long. There's a lot of empty space. The remote takes up more space on your table than it has to.

The TV is very easy to set up from start to finish. It's a nice-looking TV, and seems of good build quality. If you input a high-quality signal into the HDMI port, you'll be very happy with the picture.

The speaker quality on this TV is perfectly fine.
This Micro SD card is working as expected. Price is good.

You have the option of using alkaline batteries in the main unit and infrared sensor, or to plug them into mini-usb situation for power. The USB cables and USB charger are not included.

The color I chose does not necessarily look like just a woman's bag. It's fine if a guy wanted to do the cross strap thing and ride a bike with this.

I put on a more comfortable shoulder strap than what was provided since I knew I would sometimes be carrying heavier items.

I like the bag. It seems to be of nice quality.

There is a lot to like about this monitor. It's easily height adjustable, it can pivot, the angle can be tilted up and down, it has built-in speakers (I am using a Bose Solo 5 soundbar instead of the built-in speakers), the side and top bezels are not too wide, and the picture quality is very good, with a lot of picture configuration options. (I plugged a 3.5mm stereo patch cable from the back of the monitor into the soundbar.)

I watch TV broadcast and cable channels, movies, and TV shows via my computer, so I wanted a larger high quality-picture monitor with a higher DPI capability. I did not want to spend so much and buy one of the many monitors above $500, but I did not want one of the cheaper 32-inchers that had less DPI capability.

This LG has so far satisfied what I want. I have settled on the "HDR Effect" Picture Setting for most use, and it is quite nice. There is also a "Custom" picture setting that allows for a lot of configuration. (I could never have just settled for LG's factory default picture settings.)

The monitor is very heavy...much heavier in weight than I expected. Attaching the stand is really easy. Detaching the stand is also very easy. Build quality of this monitor seems good. Assuming this just-released monitor stays working perfectly for a long time, LG did an excellent job and I am glad I bought it.
This is perfect for using in a bathroom outlet that only has two plugs because the cord length won't take up much space.

If you are going to use this without ever using the tripod legs, it will be fine. If you need to use the tripod legs, do not buy this.

When see you're buying Bose and the $200 price, you automatically think you're going to get a crystal clear, high quality sound from this soundbar. But you don't get that.

What I got was sound that was not all that noticeably better than the speakers built into my new-model big-screen Vizio TV. Yes, I am connecting the TV to the Bose Soundbar using the optical cable. So disappointing.

And, let's not forget that unnecessarily big remote control included. It's too big and uncomfortable to hold. I hate the remote control.

Oh, and remember, there are no buttons whatsoever on the Bose Soundbar itself. If the remote ever breaks, or if it is lost, your Soundbar is useless without it.

The build quality seems solid, but what good is that if the sound quality is so subpar? Considering the disappointing sound quality, this Bose Soundbar is way overpriced. Don't get me wrong, you can hear decent sound from the TV...it's just that since it isn't much better than what you can get from your newer HD TV, why bother? Now, if you have an older inferior TV with very low-watt speakers that produce tinny sound, the Bose Soundbar will make a bigger difference for sure.

I expected so much better of a quality picture per the claims made and because of the very high price.

I have an excellent computer with HDMI output directly connected to an excellent 2017 model 1080p LED HDTV. The computer is used to stream live HDTV channels and either 720p or 1080p downloaded movies and TV show episodes, etc. (The computer puts out a resolution of 1920 x 1080 at 60 Hz, of course.)

The Darbee default setting out of the box is HiDef 100. The picture was not good at all at 100. (And I just found a video review online where the reviewer said he also could not tolerate 100 and had to turn it down to close to where I did.) I turned down the number to 75 and that helped. But the overall difference between Darbee on and off is very small at the 75 setting, and hard to like when I think about the fact it costs $200. And in fact, often the Darbee turned on was worse in the sense it accentuated flaws in the picture, especially in low light scenes.

Yes, I experimented with all 3 modes, and multiple number settings.

I am sure there are specific uses and set-ups of the Darbee where the difference in picture quality is high. But again, in my case the Darbee failed to impress me, and I cannot recommend this if your set up is like mine: computer to TV.

The Darbee is a great concept, and it is very easy to set up and use. But at $200, the value just isn't there compared with the end result I got.
Works exactly as advertised. Seems like a nice quality HDMI switch box. I like the remote control feature.

Yes, I had the initial difficulty getting it to set up after first booted. You know, where you get an error code and the advice that you should unplug and try again. You'd think after all of these years, the TiVo company would have perfected the set-up.

After a few tries, it did set up successfully.

If you are running off an antenna and want the very best DVR, and if the cost does not bother you, this Roamio OTA is the one to buy. It is so nice that cost of lifetime updates and guide is built into the price. The software is really easy to figure out and use. The TV Guide is the best there is. The tuners are high quality. If your signal is good, your picture will be great.

The TiVo is superior to other OTA DVRs like the Channel Master and the Tablo...as it should be since the cost is higher.

The suction power is almost nonexistent. The blower power is just as awful.

I have to laugh when I see at the top of the Amazon page for this item that it was reduced from nearly $26 to nearly $16.

I am telling you that this vacuum truly is terrible. Do not waste your $16 or waste your time.

This is exactly what I needed. It is worth the price. I am glad I bought it.

It is holding a heavy laptop just fine.

Easy to set up. Easy to use.
This Cat 5e cable is good quality. It does the job, as expected. I am glad I bought it.

I am giving this 5 stars for the plastic case, and 1 star for the cloths.

I do not understand why the what seems like countless companies who make microfiber cloths for eyeglasses cannot equal the superior quality and effectiveness of the genuine white Crizal cloths. (The Crizal cloths are not sold via Amazon, and are relatively expensive if you buy them from the Crizal company directly). I have tried Terrafiber and Magicfiber and many in between. (I would rate Terrafiber's cloths in second place out the many I have tried. I keep trying different cloths hoping I can find ones at Amazon that equal the Crizal cloths.)

I do not like these Spektrum cloths and do not recommend them. They do feel like they might scratch lenses, and they certainly are disappointing when it comes to cleaning.

What I do absolutely love, however, is the case Spektrum includes. I wish they sold they case separately. But since they don't, I will buy a second order of these just to have a second case to keep in my car. The case has a tiny magnetic closure. The case is perfect to hold microfiber cloths (or even pills, if you wanted.)

To the Spektrum Company: Have you considered selling the case separately?

So, again, if you want a great small case and do not mind spending $7.95 for it, I recommend this.

If you're lucky to get one that works perfectly right out of the box, this seems like it would be a decent quality DAC for the reasonable cost. (Some have reported theirs did not last long, so of course I have no idea about longevity. Mine was not working right immediately out of the box. Returned it. I did not get another one since I lost confidence in it.)

I got lucky, as this works perfectly for the device I needed it.

So far, using it 24 hours a day to power the device, it has worked reliably.

I am glad I chose to buy this one.

It is always a great feeling when the RAM you buy via Amazon works. (And once you have bought RAM that doesn't work, like I have done in the past, you'll see what I mean.)

This RAM worked. No issues so far.
The cable works. It seems well built. I recommend it. I would buy this brand again.

First of all, on the spray bottle I received the directions are completely ludicrous. The directions say to "put a drop on a small wad of tissue." Well, this is a spray bottle that spritzes out a very fine mist. There are no drops.

I have no idea why the manufacturer would put the above directions on a spray mist bottle. Makes me lose some confidence right away.

But I proceeded to ignore the label directions (since there is no way to put a drop on tissue...and doing so defeats the whole purpose of buying a spray bottle version in the first place, of course) and spray this product on my eyeglasses. I noticed a strong smell of alcohol right away.

I used a brand new, high quality microfiber cloth designed for eyeglass cleaning. I was very dissatisfied with the result. I saw streaking, and not clarity. The company included a new cloth, and I tried that as well. Same disappointing results, on 2 separate pair of glasses.

I am sorry I bought the spray.

The Formula MC version that comes in a squeeze bottle is much better, in my opinion. (I bought the spray thinking it would be as effective, but that was not the case for me. So, in the trash the bottle goes, and I am out $12.51 total ($6.35 for the item and $6.16 for shipping).

If you keep this in context regarding the fact it costs just $11, you get your money's worth for sure.

But if you want a very loud alarm built in, you'll have to spend more money than this and find an alternative.

In my opinion, the volume of the built-in alarm is not loud enough. I was disappointed with the alarm volume immediately, as I was expecting it to be louder. The volume is not scare-inducing at all.

The tiny screw they chose to use for the battery compartment is ridiculous. How many people have a tiny screw driver handy that small? Yes, of course there are some people who will have one. But I didn't.

The item feels cheap, and thus does not inspire confidence the alarm part will last a long time. Maybe it will. Maybe it won't. All I know is that it doesn't inspire confidence. (I read a review at Amazon that said the alarm part broke after 3 uses, and that it is only being used as a silent door stop now.)

But the above notwithstanding, since I love the fact this will stop the door from opening (or closing), combined with the fact it is so inexpensive and that it does have an alarm, I feel the product deserves 5 stars. (Plus, the company is very responsive and stands behind their product.)

Luckily, both cables are working as advertised. I am hoping for longevity, as we all know many 3.5mm patch cables can fail after a while.

The cables seem well constructed for their reasonable price.

I have one going from my TV's headphone jack into an expensive external speaker. The other cable is going from my iMac's headphone jack into another nice speaker. Sound quality is as expected and desired.

I put my money into getting two Spot cameras via Indiegogo back in November, 2015, and I am very happy I did. Once I received the cameras I knew right away I made the right choice. I love the Spot cameras. They work exactly as described and are of great quality.

Set up was very easy. I have the app (which is easy to use and works well) installed on my iPhone and iPad. Picture and sound quality is very good.

With the cameras being so small and light, they are easy to move to a different location, if desired.

The Spot camera is perfect for my needs. I was so happy to get a product that really works as advertised. I have had my Spots turned on 24/7 for approx. 5 months now, and have not had any negative issues.

I recommend the Spot camera. It is a good camera from a good company.

Amazon 1 Star Rating equals to "I Hate It" ... and I do have hatred for aspects of the Bolt, even though I also have love for it.

(Please keep in mind I have owned many different DVR's, such as the Moxi, ReplayTV, and Channel Master DVR+.)

I Hate:

TiVo wants a fee of $600 for a lifetime license, after you pay $300 or $400 for your Bolt. This is insanity! I could understand if they were asking for $600 for the lifetime of the person, no matter what TiVo boxes they swap out in the future.

The design of the box is terrible, in my opinion. I really hate it. (And please do not say they did it only to allow air to escape, because air can escape just fine on their Roamios and on other DVR's such as the Moxi.)

Final thing I hate is the difficulty prying the box apart to swap out the hard drive after the screws are removed. TiVo knows one's hard drive will fail eventually after the warranty, and/or that people will wanna upgrade to a larger capacity drive. They could have easily designed this box with a removable cover just under the drive, instead of making it where you have to take the whole cover off in parts.

Love:

Hands down, the TiVo interface and extra features of the Bolt are superior to any other DVR out there as of this writing. Once you have the opportunity to use Commercial Skip, you'll fall in love. Also, the Quick Mode feature is very nice, and it works well. The speed of the Bolt interface is excellent.

The TiVo software is really easy to use. The Bolt is easy to get set up. I like that if you have to swap out your hard drive, the TiVo software will automatically install itself on the bare new drive.

I like the online and mobile interfaces which allow you to set recordings remotely.

There are countless people online who feel that TiVo's $15 per month (or $150 per year) fee is too expensive ... and of course if you are paying it, you will wish the fee was a more reasonable $10 per month/$100 per year.

I am hoping TiVo has heard the endless complaints of folks who hate the Bolt's box design and who want a flat box. It will be interesting to see if they do a redesign of their next DVR model. And I'm hoping they come out with a TiVo Bolt OTA for cable cutters where the lifetime license fee will be far more reasonably priced than the Bolt's astronomical $600.

I bought my pair of Bluez 2S directly from AfterShokz company, and not via Amazon. Just like with so many things there are aspects to like and aspects to not like.

I will start with the negatives. If you are in a noisy environment, such as working out in an exercise room, the volume just is not loud enough or satisfactory at all. You need earplugs in the ears to get the satisfactory volume. Yes, earplugs. Of course, that defeats the whole purpose of buying headphones that do not go inside or cover your ears.

You can test this out by simply putting a finger in each ear and then you'll hear the remarkable level of volume change.

Because of the lack of loudness one can achieve in a noisy environment, I cannot recommend these (unless you want to buy earplugs and wear them at the same time).

The only other negative for me personally is the lack of a way to go back to a previous song, or repeat the currently playing song. (You can skip forward to the next song, but you cannot go back.)

The positives: These are comfortable to wear and very lightweight. The Bluez 2S offers the ability for decent call quality when using them to make calls. Microphones seem good (I have only tried this indoors, and not outdoors, so I cannot comment further on this particular subject.)

The Bluez 2S are very easy to operate.

In a quiet environment, volume is fine, and music quality is acceptable for this price point. (Of course you will not get the level of music quality or bass you'd get with a more expensive name brand headphones that go directly over the ear.)

So, for specific purposes such as cell phone calls where you want to keep both ears free, these are quite good indeed, offering good voice quality for both parties. (Pairing with my iPhone 5 and 6S went flawlessly.)

I bought one of those very small ASUS VivoMini UN62-M037M computers. It has an HDMI out port to connect to either a monitor or your nice HD TV. (I have mine connected to my TV.) I am running Windows 8.1 on the computer.

Microsoft has acknowledged that there is a bug in Windows 8 and 8.1: When you turn off your TV but leave your computer on, the OS will always give you an Out of Memory error message. There is no software fix whatsoever. Many people are complaining of this issue on boards over at Intel and other places.

The only fix is to either never ever turn off your TV, or always turn off your computer when you turn off your TV, or fool the computer into thinking there is that HDMI monitor connected even when said monitor is powered off.

I bought this ConnectPRO for just this purpose...and it works.

Out of the box I did not get a green light, per the instructions. The light was orange, which implies it had a memorized EDID from the factory.

I reset the box and cloned the EDID from my TV.

I can now leave my computer on always if I desire and turn off my TV at any time, and no more problems.

Sad that Microsoft never offered their own software fix via an update, in spite of the fact they confirm the issue, which forced me to have to spend an extra $70.
I installed this in a Mid-2010 iMac. So far, all is perfect, and as fast as expected. Price was great for the 250GB SSD. I would recommend.

I installed 4 sticks (4-gigs per stick) into a Mid-2010 iMac (3.06 GHz i3). All went perfectly. So far, all  is working perfectly. I did a MemTest after installation, and the RAM passed. I would say this is good quality RAM.

My specific circumstance: I wanted a computer to put next to my High-Def TV so I can play movies and TV shows, etc. My TV becomes the gorgeous computer monitor via the HDMI input. I have Ethernet right there, so I did not have to buy the additional WiFi adapter for the computer. I use a wireless keyboard and mouse.

This Asus has 4 USB 3.0 ports. I recommend this Asus model with the 4 ports instead of their model with only 2 ports.

I bought one 8-Gig RAM stick for $44 (Crucial CT102464BF160B via Amazon). I bought a 256GB mSATA drive for $103 (Crucial MX200 via Amazon). (I already had a wireless mouse [Logitech M525] and a wireless keyboard [Anker A7723].)

So, I spent about $435 total. (Luckily I already had a copy of Windows 8.1 I could use, plus a USB DVD drive. Of course, you can also install Windows via a USB Flash Drive.)

Opening up the bottom by removing the 4 screws is fast and easy. Installing the RAM and mSATA hard drive is also fast and easy.

I hooked up my HDMI cable direct from the computer to my TV and the rest went easy.

The Windows drivers are easily downloaded from Asus Website.

The computer is very quiet and small and nice. The i5 processor runs as expected. Boot times are fast. The Intel Video chip they provide is great at doing what I need it to: Provide a crystal clear picture to my TV, and allow me to stream high-def movies and TV shows from the computer.

For what I do and at the total price I paid, this Asus VivoMini is perfect. (With it seeming solidly built, I am hoping for longevity.)

This keyboard is so nice and lightweight...perfect if you are typing with the keyboard on your lap while on a sofa or recliner, etc. I paired this keyboard to a Windows 8 computer just fine, no problem at all.

Works great on a desk, too, of course.

Very easy to operate. And the price is great.

The seller is also wonderful when it comes to communication, and replied fast when I had a question.
If you need a 15-foot 3.5mm male to 3.5mm male patch cable, this one is a great choice. It appears very well constructed. I like that the cable is thin. The ends seem solid. Sound is clear.

I am shaking my head wondering why Arris would think putting in blinding blue indicator lights on this modem was a good idea! The blue upstream and downstream indicator lights on the SB6121 and SB6141 are not nearly as blinding. Why?

I am not exaggerating at all. The blue lights are blindingly bright. Do not stare into them.

Of course, I could turn the modem around, but why should I have to do that on a $130 modem?

I could put tape over the lights...but that defeats the purpose of having the indicator lights in the first place.

If your shelf or cabinet setup is such where the modem is hidden from view, this modem is fine. But if you are in a situation where your room is small and the modem has to be in sight, by all means you should avoid this modem.

Do the people at Arris not actually look at the lights after designing?

This modem is listed as compatible with Cox Communications...and I was able to get it to work with Cox at full speed. However, due to the blindingly bight blue indicator lights, I either have to hunt down a different modem, or place something in front of it to block the lights. (Or tape a piece of paper or cloth on the front, which I'd have to lift up if I want to check the lights.) I paid $130 for this modem, and I have to do that? Mind-boggling.

First I want to say that the first box I received did not work correctly immediately. The box kept failing to maintain recognition that my external drives were in fact present, no matter how many different types I used. There was surely something wrong with the ViewTV. (The ViewTV I received had software version installed from last month.)

I called the ViewTV company and they were really great. The nice tech support guy agreed I had to have something wrong with the unit...and he rushed me out a replacement. The replacement works much better...and interestingly its software version is dated 7 months ago.

I think the ViewTV at $50 is really a great value. (And I was impressed with the customer service the company provided.)

Running the antenna channel scan is relatively fast. The picture quality on my replacement box is stellar. Moving through all the settings menus is very easy and straightforward. Everything is easy to figure out.

When you think about the box's limitations, as pointed out by some very helpful reviews here, you must keep in mind the very reasonable price.

For $50 you get a good over the air box with a good tuner that sends a great picture via HDMI to your TV. You can time shift your viewing, if you plug in a drive to the USB port, and you can record programs to said drive.

For $50 you cannot expect multiple tuners or a great TV Guide. But at least you get to see the very basic guide info the broadcasters send down with their OTA signal. (My two HDTV's on their own do not show the OTA program info, which is very disappointing.)

For cable cutters out there on a budget, this box is definitely something you should consider. It delivers really well exactly what it promises.

I assure you, if you do a side by side comparison between this O2 Hurricane Special Edition and a typical canned air duster you will see a huge difference, and you will be disappointed like I was.

Dusting off a TV or computer screen or eyeglasses is a good test with this and the canned air side by side, of course, but you could simply just shoot the air on your hand and feel the inferior force from the O2 Hurricane Special Edition.

I was so hoping the O2 would be better than it is because like everyone I dislike the possible frostbite situation when using the canned air. Plus, the ability to use the O2 from any angle is really nice.

One day I do expect they will be able to make a canless air system in this kind of compact cordless size that has the air blowing power we need. But until that day, unfortunately, this one just isn't it.

I got mine for $248 plus sales tax with the immediate $50 reduction in price if one has Amazon Prime. I think that is a fair price for this Soundbar.

There is a lot to like about this Soundbar. You will love its easy ability to program in your TV's remote control, or any IR remote, to control the volume and mute. Very convenient.

The volume on the Soundbar can get plenty loud. The sound is quite clear.

Vizio includes all possible cables you might need.

The Soundbar is heavy and appears solidly built.

Programming features via the Vizio remote are very nice and easy to understand and figure out.

The negative: I applaud Vizio for trying to include bass speakers into the Soundbar so you won't need a separate bass speaker, but sadly they have failed. I did lots of testing on various TV feeds, from Music Choice stations to movies to local newscasts to regular network TV shows. I did adjustments to the bass via the remote on all TV feeds. The bass level is not there yet to satisfy.

I plugged in an 8" Energy brand powered bass speaker (this is not a large bass speaker), and let me tell you the difference is remarkable with all the TV feeds.

I will strongly suggest that if you consider buying this Soundbar you accept that for the most satisfying sound you really need and should have an external bass speaker. You will not be sorry at all.

One day a company might be able to invent a Soundbar with built-in bass speakers that truly deliver. Vizio has not succeeded with this model. But again, excluding the bass aspect, the rest of the Soundbar does deliver the quality.

The Hosa YRA-104 RCA Male to Dual RCA Female Cable works exactly as advertised and as expected. Seems well built. Sound is fine. Good price. Good value. I can only report that the cable does indeed work and is doing its job.

First, a warning for you about the warranty. This Speaker Tower is very, very heavy. Should it break during the one-year warranty, as expected you will have to pay to ship it to Pyle. (I am OK with this.) But along with the item you must include a $50 money order to pay Pyle Audio to send the item back to you.

Most companies work by you pay to ship the broken item to them, they pay to ship the fixed item back to you under the warranty period.

OK, now to the product review:

Overall, I am disappointed with the quality of the audio and I do not recommend this item to people who want the best audio quality and I would not ever purchase it again.

If anyone out there paid even close to the full retail list price of $433.99, you have my sympathy.

This tower does have some positives. The ability to play either FM radio, an iOS device, or other music source (you will need a 3.5mm to dual RCA male cable if wanting to play directly from the headphone jack of an MP3 player, etc.). It would have been nice if they had included a 3.5mm input jack as well, especially at this price.

Some songs sound pretty good, but others sound muffled or muddy. Not crystal clear like you would expect at this weight and price, and from Pyle Audio. If you compare your songs through this tower and then through the $300+ Dr. Dre Original Model Beatbox as one wild example, you will hear the difference in clarity and quality from the speakers immediately.

But again, some songs do sound quite decent, and with that I can see why some give this tower a great review. But if you are like me and you want and recognize the best quality sound, you might be disappointed with this tower.

The instruction manual is very disappointing, as well. I, and most can figure things out eventually, but there will be some folks who might need to ask for help.

The FM antenna is a small hard wired wire. You cannot add your own antenna.

I got the black matte model, and it does look nice in the room.

I think this deserves 3 stars because I think there are some people who will enjoy this tower and its features and its small footprint and its look for the $171 price.

This laptop light is perfect for mobile DJ's who use laptops. With its flexibility, I can easily bend the light to either illuminate my laptop keyboard or my mixer. And the light is just the right brightness for the job.

I have tested other laptop lights and I like this one the best. It truly is perfect for my specific needs and I am glad I bought it.

I like that it has an on/off switch, but I usually keep it on all the time.

I use a $100 external sound card when DJ'ing because I want better sound than what the built-in laptop sound card offers. I notice a big difference.

I then was doing more research and read how the makers of these way more expensive USB cables claim they offer superior sound. So, I took the plunge and spent $50 for this Pangea Audio solid silver USB cable.

I seriously could not hear any difference between this USB cable and the $10 short USB cable I was using. For $50, I expected a perceptible difference, even if it was just a small difference.

I had others also judge...and they agreed with me.

From looking at and holding the cable, it does indeed come across as a quality cable. But again, I heard no difference in the sound...and I tested it with different genres of songs.

I would not recommend this cable. If you indeed have a great (and expensive) external sound card or a great DAC, my guess is you do not need to buy one of these $50 (or even more expensive) USB cables.

I give the cable 5 stars for build quality and 1 star for its inability to cause the sound from your laptop to either an external sound card or DAC to be noticeably improved. (So, I averaged it out to 3 stars.)

(I have not tested the much more expensive than this one USB cables, so maybe those do produce a perceptible difference?)

I got the 16 gigabyte HP Touchpad for $116 grand total and let me tell you it truly is a steal at that price. Do not believe anyone who says even at that low price they think the Touchpad is not worth it.

Once the Touchpad arrived, I did the system updates and all is great.

I am very happy I got one at that price and will use it a lot. If anyone can get this Touchpad for that price, I feel it is a must-purchase for anyone who wants full-Web access.

(I bought two of these Vertex 3 SSD's...this one and the Max IOPS one).

I installed this SSD in a laptop. When the laptop goes to sleep (or if I put it to sleep), the drive will not wake up. I have to press and hold the power button to shut off the computer.

OCZ released a firmware update for the Vertex 3's that might fix this issue (among other issues) fairly quickly after the drive was released, but there is no way to upgrade the firmware on my drives.

OCZ blocks firmware upgrading if the Vertex 3 SSD is the Windows Boot Drive (which it is, of course, in my laptops).

OCZ also blocks upgrading the firmware if the SSD is connected to a USB to SATA adapter.

So, I have no way whatsoever to upgrade the firmware. I do not own a tower where I could connect the drive to a secondary SATA controller. (And honestly, I shouldn't have to do that in the first place.)

The specifications imply that this tablet is designed to accept a wireless sim card if the user decides to add an additional wireless telephone line. After spending half a day trying to register my purchase with Dell, I was told that, since Dell itself was not the seller, they are not bound to provide warranty coverage. So, Amazon Warehouse buyers might want to figure a Square Trade or other third-party warranty into the purchase price for this Dell. When I asked about the fact that a card slot for a wireless phone sim card is engineered into the Dell Venue, the Dell rep informed me that the Dell engineers originally designed a separate card slot for this purpose, but "in recent models it has been DISCONNECTED!" Which is just about the most nonsensical thing I've heard in a long time.

Several years ago, I worked as a technical telephone support person for Denon home theater systems, and realized at that time that audio and telecommunications engineers frequently make completely mystifying. unnecessarily complicated design decisions, so this was not news to me ....It WAS however, a disappointment that cost the Dell Venue 8 two stars on this review.

That said, the 2GHz processor and Jelly Bean OS are wicked fast for simple gaming, texting (with "My SMS" or other texting apps from Google Play, synched to your Android phone), etc. It can be synchronized via Wi-Fi, USB tether or Bluetooth. It's a nice size (although a little heavy), and makes a very good Kindle-type unit for reading news, books, online magazines, etc. I've decided I like the tablet very much, but would be a LOT happier with if I could get Dell updates and downloads or install a wireless phone card.

I just received this Sanjean RCR-10 and set it up. The good news is that the sound is wonderfully rich and balanced for a little radio. First bedside table clock radio I've ever had that sounds good enough to crank up loud to fill my whole apartment with music. I'm impressed, and I'm not easily impressed.

On the other hand, it seems that, the more sophisticated these digital electronics get, the more challenging and puzzling they are to set up. It could well be that these companies need to shell out a little more money for decent technical writers to produce more thorough step-by-step setup instructions. OR, they could simply design the units so they're easier to set up for those of us who are not geeks or electronics engineers. It's not all that terribly frustrating; just be ready for several minutes of trial and error ...and pray you don't have a power outage! (The unit also offers a back-up batteries feature, so I wouldn't forget to do that.)

The RCR-10 is solid, substantial (not flimsy or lightweight) and attractive. The display also includes basic metadata indicating station and artist. The only thing missing for me --since I use an Android phone as my personal music player-- would be a little close-able cover for the empty iPod docking slot. It's going to be a dust collector in my house.

Everywhere I looked online, there were nothing but the highest words of praise for this radio. It's an attractive, compact unit, with reasonably good sound and lots of options for add ons, additional speakers, usb ports, etc. However, I had such a difficult time getting it to find my home network, I had to completely reconfigure my router (and two computers as a consequence) in order to get the radio to "find" my home network and accept my password key. The enclosed setup instructions are so inadequate that most of the information and procedures required to sign up for services like Pandora, I Heart Radio, Rhapsody, NPR, etc., were completely missing from the manual. The only indications of how to start appeared in the radio's display window, instructing me to go online to do the setup. After some perseverance, I finally figured out how to use the Reciva Internet Radio site to connect the radio with the services I've been using with my computers for years.

Once I finally got the thing to start streaming (about 4 frustrating hours after I began the set up) I realized that, even less than three feet from my router, the unit stayed in buffering mode more than it actually played music, no matter what bps settings I tried. I don't really know much about the technical end of audio streaming, but my MediaLink router works fine with my two portable computers, and streams video and music from services like Pandora and Rhapsody with no glitches whatever. I didn't see much point in listening to 10 seconds of a song, then waiting through 15 or 20 while the unit's memory silently buffered so it could continue.

Even if you're not a digital audio newbie, if you're looking for straightforward setup and easy operation, this AIN'T IT. I may look further into wireless digital radio --but I doubt it, at least not in the near future.

I was looking to upgrade my gaming mouse. I was excited to try this one, but when I got it plugged in, there were two things that immediately upset me. First, it didn't use the Logitech SetPoint software all my other Logitech devices have used for many, many years. Instead, I had to install a new software to customize the buttons. Second, the mouse acceleration I've become accustomed to was eliminated from this mouse in the software. In its place, they added a "precision mode" button that required me to take my thumb off the trackball to toggle between fast movement and slow movement. As a gamer, this is unacceptable. I loved everything else about this mouse, but it didn't work for me, since my primary use is gaming.
I have astigmatism, so for me, it was impossible to "dial in" either lens for a good viewing experience, let alone both. I was really excited to try it and very sad it didn't work for me.

The extra buttons (back and forward) are in an awkward place. For me, that meant I could either be using those or the ball. As a mouse for things like browsing the web, checking email, watching movies, etc. it wasn't bad. It just isn't laid out to make an effective gaming mouse.

Initially, I liked the ergonomic design. It put much less pressure on my wrist than the Logitech trackball I've been using for many years. Unfortunately, when I started up World of Warcraft, I noticed the Kensington trackball button mapping software disabled the ability to use more than one button at once. I found the same detriment in Overwatch where multiple buttons often need to be pressed simultaneously. When I contacted the company, they sent me an email. The following is a direct quote from their email:
"Thank you for contacting Kensington Technical Support.

We would like to inform you that these trackballs are designed for basic office use and will not work on gaming applications.

We appreciate your time and patience."

To me, this came across as rather rude. This, coupled with the fact that this very mouse shows up in searches for gaming trackball mouse made me extremely disappointed and, in fact, somewhat angry. I feel Kensington needs to do any or all of the following. 1. Fix the software to make their hardware gaming inclusive. 2. Stop advertising their non-gaming devices as gaming devices (I feel this is blatant false advertising.) 3. Ask customers how they could fix issues rather than giving them a short, curt email to inform us that we, apparently, are idiots for expecting their devices to work as advertised.

Bottom line: I do not recommend buying this product unless all you intend to use it for is emails and youtube.

This review is for the Uniden BCD436HP I see reviews here for other radios, so not to be confused.
I used Amazon Prime Now to get the radio to me, in less than 1 hour (about 45 minutes) the delivery person was knocking on my door with my new receiver, wow, I was highly impressed and I will always check to see if Prime Now is available for all my deliveries from now on.....
So, the radio....
This receiver has a 4 gig SD card preloaded with every known frequency with text for the entire US and Canada. They have software called Sentinel you install on your PC and this is your gateway to all updates and firmware and it can control your radios SD card any way you like. Sentinel has an extensive database of all frequencies and let me say this again, all frequencies have text description included which is the most highly advanced scanner database system I have ever seen and I have owned scanner receivers most of my adult life, (long time)..
This is a digital receiver using the latest technology available. It can monitor any analog or digital TX (with some exceptions, like encrypted signals) and gives you extensive control over what you're listening to. There are FCC laws regarding what is legal and not legal to monitor and Uniden has got us right up to the maximum legally allowed to be monitored by civilians. If you are law enforcement persons you will have much more powerful receivers available to you capable of Cell phone conversation monitoring etc., things no civilian should even be interested in.
There is another version of this Uniden radio, the BCD536 which is a tabletop version. If you have large powerful outdoor weatherproof antennas the BCD536 is a good option and it is completely transferable to vehicle dash mount and back from your work desk to your vehicle.
I like this handheld BCD436 best personally for my purposes.
This is basically a plug and play receiver. It comes with 3 2300 milliamp rechargeable batteries, load those, charge them or just leave radio plugged in, enter your zip and you're in. Well theoretically that's how it works, in the real world? No.
When you first receive the radio I would suggest positioning yourself in front of your PC. Have the paper manual, the radio, you and your PC right there in front of you. Get ready to read and learn your radios keyboard layout and what these great, well thought out keys can do for you. You will learn, trust me, you will quickly come to love this radio.
Some cons:
No wall charger adopter included. You can charge from your PC's USB ports but you will need a wall charger with USB port. Most of us have several of these around the house from old cell phones etc. They work fine.
This unit should come with a nice wall charger adopter. That's really the only con, not to bad really.
Antennas:
Your ability to scan and receive signals on any scanner is proportionate to your antennas. The more robust and correct (correct meaning size, materials used etc).. You will need some nice antennas for this nice radio to increase your scanning powers. Amazon has some nice antennas, scannermaster.com has some also. Your local radio shop retailer will have some also. The included rubber ducky antenna is garbage, toss it from across the room to your garbage can, see if you can make a rim shot. Like I said, I have been playing with scanners for many years so I have many antennas to pick from.
Verdict:
This is without a doubt, the most powerful handheld scanning receiver available from any manufacturer. It is the luxury sedan of the scanning receiver world. It is easy and robust. It is backed up by Uniden's Sentinel software which will future proof your radio for many years to come.
I give Uniden 5 stars for this winner.
I give Amazon 5 stars for Prime Now 1 hour shipping, also a winner.

Edit:
Okay some people are wondering what the best accessories are for this receiver.
Go to scannermaster.com and look for the Austin Condor All-Band Portable BNC Antenna and the SpectrumForce Desk Mount for One Portable Scanner.
The Condor all band antenna is unsurpassed.
The desktop stand holds your handheld at the perfect viewing angle, you can listen and see all text clearly right beside your computer.

I have put together many, many computers using cases of all shapes, sizes and costs. Dollar for dollar this case is hands down the best value I've ever seen. And I like that is fairly light weight, many cases that are "sturdy" are also on the heavy side. By the time you have them loaded with a good power supply and several hard drives they begin to feel like a tank when you need to move them.

The cutouts and gaps to make routing cables easy are nice, they not only improve the appearance but also help air flow freely through the case. I was a little worried about sharp edges but have not found any, which is good because knowing me if there was even one I would have cut myself on it.

I read several reviews which mention the hard drive rails being difficult and backwards so I wasn't sure what to expect. At first I was a little confused about how the hard drives are meant to be installed but once I understood it, it makes perfect sense and is no problem to work with. If you have right angled power and data cable ends you can mount the drives facing left or right which might make things easier if you have several drives installed.

Another thing that both surprised and pleased me was when I was installing the power supply I noticed there were two extra holes which makes it possible to mount the ps either right side up or upside down. I am not a huge fan of bottom mount for power supplies and as others have said, it can cause problems if the leads for motherboard power are not long enough. Mine just barely reached to the cpu power connector after running it up the rear of the case, resting as it is on the motherboard and running under the video card. I have extensions on order though I'm sure I could get by for the life of the ps as it is now.

I like the long, thin blue light on the front for power on though the green light for hard drive activity is a bit hard to see. Most of all though, I love the paint. No more of that ugly, dingy looking gray metal with thoughts of how I want to paint it black. I am not an expert on such things but I believe the paint is baked on giving it a very nice texture and appearance.

Besides their sound and level of ANC. i liked the fact the Sony earbuds still had a lot of playback control available from the earbuds and you can use either earbud individually. I also felt like the fact that they sit in your ear canal rather than on the outside would contribute to the noise cancellation.

The earbuds felt and sound good and the accompanying app was nice but the case had a cheap, almost cardboard feel. My main issues were, although the earbuds never actually fell out of my ear, I think their top-heavy design made them feel like they were always about to fall out. The bigger issue i had, which won't apply to everyone, is how much effort went into getting them to sit correctly in my ear. Even with twisting, and pushing, I could never get the right earbud to fit securely in my ear like the left one did.

After a day of wearing the Sonys i decided to pick up a pair of Bose Quietcomfort ear buds as i already had a pair of Quietcomfort 35 over the ears that i loved, i figured I'd give Bose another shot. As soon as i opened the Bose, I immediately fell in love. Besides the unboxing and charging case feeling more premium, the earbuds went into my ear effortlessly and securely. I wore them the first day and they stayed in place all day and sounded great.

Although the Sony WF-1000XM4 is a great set of earbuds, The Bose earbuds have the same functionality, sound and ANC but are designed in a way to comfortably fit a wider array of ear shapes and at a cheaper price. The Sonys are going back and the Bose are going to be my new day-to-day earbuds.

All crystal clear pictures. I must say that most towers are about 40 miles away from my home ,all kinda clustered together. They sit southeast of me and where I have the antenna sitting is close to southeasterly. Kind of a no brainer but I would suggest looking up tower locations  in your area. The map will display channels broadcast by this tower... and try to configure your antenna in that general direction. Makes sense to me. Very pleased with this antenna and purchase. Cut the cord with cable. You won't be disappointed :) UPDATE: This is an indoor antenna and they work best in a window and pointed towards the transmission towers in your area. You will get max channels that way. That's been my experience but I opted to use the double stick tape provided and mount mine outside taped to a beam on my metal pergola. Channel availability jumped up immediately upon rescanning so outdoor antennas are the way to go...and yes this is not truly recommended for outdoor use.. I went from 36 channels inside to 55 mounted outside the same window..3 months and I have had no issues with outside use. It hasn't fallen once..the weather has been all over the map..from sunny, rainy, and even the current blizzard conditions we have experienced...that includes rain, freezing rain, and snow. Maybe it will crap out over time but I paid 15 bucks for over 50channels. If it lasts a year thats only $1.25 a month to watch tv which is hella lot cheaper than cable. I'm super satisfied!!
