This seems like a fairly average keyboard with nothing to make it stand out above the crowd. There are some issues involved with it though that you should be aware of before buying. The first issue is general one with all wireless keyboards, a matter of the trade-off involved in going wireless. The advantages of a wireless keyboard and mouse are that they reduces the clutter of wires on your desk and they are more portable than their wired kin. The main disadvantage is that they need either regular batteries or regular recharging, either of which is just extra maintenance that wired equipment doesn't need. Only you can decide if the trade-off is worth it or not to you.

There is a big issue specific to this keyboard though that you should be aware of. The keys on this board come in three colors - red, grey, and black. The lettering on the black keys is done in white which makes them easy to read. The lettering on the red and grey keys though is done in a grey tone that is hard to see. Even though the keyboard is done in a fairly standard layout, the difficulty in seeing the lettering really is a pain. So, all in all, this is not a terrible keyboard but it's not a great one either, and I have to give it an average 3 star rating.

I had a keyboard die when I spilled liquid on it so I grabbed the first one I saw available without looking at the details. When I opened the box and found that this was a backlit keyboard with large print keys, I was intrigued. As an old, retired guy, I spend hours a day at the computer gaming, streaming videos, and staying in touch with a far-flung network of family and friends via social media. This keyboard is particularly nice for the gaming. The white backlight against the black keyboard, as well as the large print keys make it very easy for me to hit the right keys when my eyes are bouncing back and forth between the screen and the keyboard while my hands are handling the both the keyboard and the mouse. This keyboard makes my responses faster and more accurate, which I very much appreciate as an older gamer.

There are those irritating glitches though. One of the worse is that the backspace key constantly sticks. Thankfully, I don't use that key in my gaming, or this keyboard would be totally unusable for me. When typing things like this review though, or posts on social media, that sticky key is very frustrating. Every time I have to backspace to clear a mistake I have to hit that key repeatedly, like I had to do three times while typing this sentence. What makes it even worse is that there is no telling how many hits it takes to move back the necessary amount of spaces. So it is very easy to backspace too far, causing even more mistakes.

Another glitch is that the keys seem bigger than on my last keyboard. I don't notice that in gaming, but when typing more than a few sentences of text, my hands and fingers begin to feel some strain. There are some minor glitches too. The volume control on my speakers is in an awkward place to reach. My last keyboard had separate volume control keys, making it easy to adjust the volume from the keyboard. This one also has volume controls but they are on the function keys, requiring two buttons to be pressed to raise or lower the volume. That sounds like a small thing but every time I adjust the volume,it is a bit irritating to have to hit two keys instead of one. And finally, this keyboard bills itself as "quiet". Hah! It's probably the nosiest, clackity clack typing I've done in a long, long time.

All in all, this keyboard feels like a cheaper knockoff of a higher quality one. For now I'll use this one, because I need it. As soon as I find that higher quality keyboard though, this one is getting tossed out.

This is the third tablet I've tried recently. On the plus side, it has some nice accessories that didn't come with the other two tablets. Those include a case, a stylus, and a screen protector. For the Fire and other Android tablets I tried, those all had to be bought separately. I did have some practical issues with this tablet though. The more serious one is that I have trouble keeping it charged up. Sometimes it seems to charge just fine. Other times I can't get it to turn on. A lesser but still irritating issue was with the stylus. When first setting up the tablet I had a lot of trouble entering the passcode for my wifi server. A dozen times I was unable to get the code loaded even though I was being careful to enter it correctly. It turned out that the stylus was, for some unknown reason, entering a symbol I had never seen before instead of an s. When I used my fingers, instead of the stylus, to enter the code, it worked perfectly and I was finally able to connect the tablet to the internet. I don't know if the stylus and the charging glitches are something I am doing wrong or some problem with this tablet, so I'm giving it a neutral three star rating. Check the other reviews. If I am the only one having these issues, then it's likely just me. If, on the other hand, others are reporting similar problems, you may want to hesitate about buying this product.

The tablet came charged, which was nice, but the problems started very quickly after first turning it on. After connecting my email and turning on a YouTube video, the tablet kicked me off in a few minutes. It then glitched when trying to turn it back on, taking something like 45 tries before it actually started working again. I'm watching another video right now and the image is grainy while the audio is tinny. Photos taken with the built in camera are also very grainy and poor quality. If you need a cheap tablet and have low expectations for it, this might work. If you need a quality product though, pass on this one.

EDIT: After a few days of usage, this tablet finally crashed and won't turn back on again. It is now worthless and I am dropping my rating to 1 star to reflect that sad reality.

As an old retired guy, there are a couple of techie things that are a big part of my life. One is that I spend hours every day gaming online in my favorite MMO. The other is that I use social media keep in touch with family members who live all around the U.S. I got this tablet to keep next to my desktop pc just so it could give me notifications when messages came in from family members. That way, the notifications wouldn't directly disrupt my gaming but they would let me know to check social media when I wasn't in the middle of some major boss fight or the like. This tablet failed miserably at that simple task. By the second day, the notifications stopped giving the audio signal. Then the tablet kept going to sleep so I couldn't even check the notifications visually. And no, I couldn't find a way to just turn off the sleep function. I finally gave up on this Amazon tablet and instead got an Android one. The new tablet works like a charm, giving me exactly what I wanted - timely, non-disruptive notifications that a family member had sent me something. The sleep function is turned off. The audio notification signal is working just fine. And now I can respond to my family fairly quickly.

As a casual gamer who is very much not a part of the hard core, "git gud" crowd that feels the need to squeeze every ounce of perfect performance out of themselves and their gear. I play for the chill fun of it. Still I would like to be as effective as possible so I took a look at this mouse. The major attraction of it for me was the 12 extra programmable buttons. I play a complex MMO that uses a lot of keybinding to make the game easier and quicker to play. Sadly, those 12 programmable buttons were the very thing that turned me off about this mouse. They are not, contrary to other gaming mice I've seen, new buttons. The first 9 buttons on the side of this mouse simply duplicate the number pad found on most keyboards. So I've already got important keybindings on all those numbers. Thus, the side of this mouse only offers me 3 new buttons to program and they are in the most awkward spot.

Even worse, this mouse was not at all ergonomic for me. The side buttons are placed where my thumb normally rests on other mice. Instinctively, my thumb curled up away from those buttons and/or tried to rest on them very gently. Within a few minutes of using this mouse, I could feel my thumb getting sore in ways that don't happen when I game for hours on a regular mouse.

I'm giving this product a neutral 3 star rating because these things may or may not be an issue for other folks. All I can suggest is that you read a variety of the reviews here to decide for yourself if you want to try this mouse or not.

The idea is a good one. Given that on my desk I have two computer towers, two monitors, two sets of speakers, and four external hard drives, the area behind my computers/monitors is an unsightly mess of tangled cords and such. So a way of organizing that clutter seemed like it would be helpful. Sadly, this product didn't work for me.  For one thing, my power strip has two rows of four sockets rather than one long strip. It's simply too wide for this box. For another thing, the bottom of the box was cracked. Looking at the other reviews, it seems several people had boxes that had issues of one kind or another. Given the size problem I didn't go to the bother of returning mine but those who did seem to have gotten a satisfactory response from the company. The idea itself is a good one. The box has an attractive appearance and the use of renewable materials is a plus. So I have to give this product a neutral 3 star rating. A couple of weeks ago I got a monitor stand to use on my desk. It had a large circular hole on the back of the monitor shelf along with a plastic cover for the hole. Apparently the idea was to give a discreet place to run the monitor's plug through. That seemed like a silly waste to me as you could just run the plug off the back of the stand with much less hassle. So the idea of this product, using that hole for a charger with some extra USB connections, seemed like a good idea to me. A real caveat though is that there are several essential details to pay attention to in using this item.

The first essential detail is to pay attention to the size of the hole you are going to use this on and the size of this product. Apparently those holes are not a standard size and some folks have had issues using this item because of that. Handyman types who have the tools to enlarge a grommet hole have an advantage here but it would behoove everyone to make sure this product will fit what they need.

The second detail to notice is that this device only works with USB 3.0 devices. The 2.0 ones won't work. My desktop computer has both 2.0 and 3.0 USB plugs. You can plug any device into any of those slots and it will work although the speed may vary. A 2.0 device plugged into a 3.0 slot will run but at 2.0 speeds. With this product, the 2.0 devices won't work at all.

The final detail to watch out for may be the most important one. Several people who have plugged the charger into their computer have reported difficulties it's created with their machines. So if you want to do that, pay very close attention the first time you try it to avoid any problems.

As an old, retired guy I spend a lot of time online gaming, streaming videos, and dabbling on social media. Over the last few months I've tried out a variety of keyboards and mice, some of them high end gaming gear. As soon as you take this keyboard and mouse out of the box it's clear that this is a low end rig. It just doesn't have the solid heft of more expensive equipment. That's not necessarily a bad thing though as I've used some excellent, inexpensive keyboards and mice. Sadly, this product is not of that caliber either.

The compact size makes the keyboard feel cramped when typing. Even as I'm writing this, my fingers are feeling strained from the cramped tightness. The manufacturer makes the 12 function/F key combos seem like a big deal. To me those combos just seem like an unnecessary complication. There are other, more standard ways of doing all those things without having to learn a whole new set of keys. The six "hot keys" seem to be just a set of video controls that duplicate functionality already available on any computer with a standard video player.

The mouse is particularly disappointing for anyone who does gaming. Now I'm just a casual gamer, by no means a hard core one, and even I find this mouse to be a handicap. In my main game you move your character forward by holding down both the left and right mouse buttons simultaneously. With other mice that is no big deal. With this mouse there is a perceptible hesitation or stutter before moving when holding down the buttons like that. That may not sound like a big deal to a non-gamer but that kind of stuttering can quickly get your character killed in a gaming battle. Also, it seems to take some effort to hold those buttons down. My fingers feel a strain in holding these mouse buttons down, a strain I haven't felt with other mice. And yes, I did try the suggested solutions for mouse problems offered in the "Manual" that came with this product (one tiny sheet printed on both sides). They didn't help.

So if you are mostly watching videos and reading Facebook on your computer, you will probably be okay with this gear. Any more serious use than that and you will want to pass on this stuff.

The need for an uninterruptible power source is obvious to anyone with a computer or other expensive electronic equipment. The very day this product arrived, before I even opened the box, a severe thunderstorm knocked out power in my neighborhood. My two computers immediately went down and the screen on one kept flashing on and off even after all the power was dead. So yes, a UPS seems like an important piece of equipment these days. Sadly, this one is not for me. To be fair to the manufacturer though I need to give you a bit of context to help you evaluate if my reaction and this review would be applicable to you or not.

At age 70 I have a pretty low tolerance for muss and fuss. If it requires special handling, if it is a hassle to use, I don't want it. If it's not plug and play, I won't bother with it. For example, I do all my laundry in one load throwing everything in together without any sorting of any kind. It all gets washed and dried on the hot cycle. Anything that can't handle that gets tossed out. I treat everything like that. This UPS looks like an industrial strength product but acts like a delicate little snowflake. Coming out of the box it has 20 pages of instructions they want you to read before using. I didn't bother, just plugged it in, turned it on, and starting using the USB charger to juice up a battery run children's night light. A little while later I noticed a burnt plastic smell and saw the warping on the case that you can see in the attached photos. So this thing is not for me. More detail oriented and careful folks might have better luck with it. Thus I'm giving it a neutral 3 star rating and suggest you read through all the reviews here before deciding whether you want to try it yourself or not.

What I thought I was getting was a competent mid-level machine that could comfortably replace a four year computer that was barely limping along anymore. What I actually got was a useless piece of junk far worse than the decrepit computer it was meant to replace. From the day I took it out of the box there were problems. Opening files, moving or copying them are all painfully slow. Even deleting files takes a long, dragged out time. Programs freeze even if I'm only running one. Forget running multiple programs at once - the machine just locks up. Videos stutter and freeze. Music stops and starts. The list of slow, clunky issues goes on and on. Even worse is the bugginess. If I switch jacks between speakers and headphones, no sound comes out and the indicators tell me no audio output is plugged in even though one clearly is. It takes 2-3 reboots before the computer figures out that yes, the speakers really are plugged in. Then there's the internet - or the lack thereof. At first I kept getting constant disconnects. That deteriorated to the point where now I can't log in at all. The wifi indicator says I'm connected at full strength. The network troubleshooter says there are no problems. All drivers are up to date. The firewall rules are correctly set. Norton Security, Windows Defender and Malwarebytes all say there is nothing bad lurking in my system. All of that and the machine simply won't connect. The Chrome browser just keeps saying websites can't load, pages can't open, because there is no internet connection. (This review is being written on another computer logged into the same network, one that connects just fine. So the issue is not the router, the isp provider or anything like that.)

As a 69 year old with significant physical issues, the thought of reboxing this piece of junk up and hauling it to a shipper to return it feels overwhelming. (My mailman carried it in for me and helped me unbox it.) Originally I had intended to just keep plodding along with it until I could save enough on my limited social security check to replace it. Given the fact that I can't even get online with it anymore though, I am going to have to figure out how to return it. The saddest part is that I have had Acer equipment before that worked just fine. Maybe this one got dropped on its head in shipping or something. I dunno, but I do know it has got to go.

EDIT: And the return process through UPS was a horrific mess. I stopped at the UPS store a couple of days ahead of time to ask them if they could box the computer and monitor up for me if I brought in all the original boxes and packing material. The nice young man working that afternoon said of course though he would have to charge me a dollar for tape. Two days later when I brought everything to the store, a different staff member said they had to charge me $30 for boxes even though I had brought the boxes in. Not only that, but I had forwarded the shipping label to that UPS store via email. They couldn't open the label so I had to go home, print out a screenshot of the label and send them that. The kicker though was that I couldn't leave the computer and monitor at the store while I ran home, ten minutes away. The clerk insisted that I carry it all out to the car again and then carry it back into the store when I returned. For somebody of my age with my health issues, that is not a trivial thing. The last time I tried to return something through UPS they gave me such a run around that I ended up throwing the item away rather than return it to Amazon. The hassle was more than the product was worth. If I ever have to return anything again, I'll ask Amazon if I can do it through Fed Ex or the Post Office. UPS is too much hassle.

Ok so this product did what it advertises, I could film underwater. Could I film clearly underwater? No. Not at all.
I'm fairly certain the reason this product does not work is the distance between the lens and the case. Here's what's wrong with the case...

All of my underwater footage from my recent trip (probably around 5-6 hours total), is completely useless and blurry. The camera can't focus through the casing.

The casing also doesn't repel water droplets well enough, rendering the camera incapable of focusing on any objects if it's wet at all. Even a small dip in the water will leave the camera struggling after it's brought to the surface.

Aside from the focusing issues, the inability to access the screen was more frustrating than I expected. The DJI Osmo Pocket is heavily reliant on the menu options only accessed by the touch screen. Without the screen, the options are extremely limited.

Would not suggest, ESPECIALLY for the insane price.

As someone who love cheap thrills, I can say I am glad I got this over the expensive gimble.

All in all, it really depends on your desired shot. Pick this for speed, gimble for everything else.

My first thought when I initially saw the Motorola Sphere 2-in-1Bluetooth Speaker with Over-Ear Headphones was, wow. It is extremely attractive and would definitely appeal to the young folks. Ironically, our house is full of loud, music playing teenagers who have very clear ideas about what sounds good and which products they prefer to use. They like speakers and headphones that offer clear sound quality with bass. We have a Bose Soundlink speaker, and VModa or Sennheiser earphones. So unfortunately when I reviewed these, I was comparing them with others that I have used. While this product might look good (definitely a 5), it needs to sound good. And this is where I am disappointed – in the sound quality.
In a nutshell:

Attractiveness – The Motorola Sphere is attractive. It is black and looks like a head with headphones.The system looks nice on a bookshelf, desk or dresser in a dorm room, bedroom, etc.. I do love the look.

Set up – The directions for setting up the device are easy to follow. Once you pair the headphones and the sphere (separately) to your phone (via Bluetooth), it is pretty easy to use. There is sometimes a lag when you disconnect or switch between the sphere and the headphones. You might have to press the button on the headphones to make the sound switch between the two devices.

Headphones – They are adjustable and the sound quality is good via the headphones.

Sound Quality – The sound quality is not good thru the speaker. I’d give it 2.5 at the most. To me the frequency response seemed a little high, which is why the sound thru the speaker is hollow or missing something, no matter the genre (i.e., classic, jazz, rap, rock) played. But a plus is that the quality of the sound thru the headphones is better, it is more balanced and therefore rates 3.5-4 (although the bass is still not heavy).

In conclusion, while I love the look and concept (2 in 1 – speaker and headphones) of the Motorola, I wouldn’t recommend it. I would instead suggest investing a little more money and getting a better more quality speaker.

When I was reading about this product, I was intrigued. The Belkin charging dock duo can charge two devices: an IPAD (4th generation), IPAD Mini/AIR, Nano (7th generation), IPOD Touch (5th generation) or an Iphone (5 or up), at the same time. Surely this is a useful item to own. Well, I was mistaken.

Usefulness: While you would think that this product is useful....because it can charge multiple devices at once... it is also a little burdensome. It's bulky, so I would not recommend this product while traveling. On the other hand, if you use the charging cables/cords that come with the devices, you can wrap them up and store them in a small compartment in your bag. This docking station would take up space in a travel bag, briefcase or suitcase. However, I would recommend this product for those who want to charge multiple "I" devices on their nightstand or dressers. I do like that they can be charged standing up, which makes them neater and more orderly. On a positive note, you can use your device while it is charging. Why you would want to I don't know, but it is an option.

Functionality: There is a handy, dandy ball that you can roll with your finger that allows you to raise and lower the adapter (front compartment and back), in order to accommodate a phone with a cover. The instructions suggest that you remove the cover to charge, but for the average consumer that would be inconvenient to remove the cover every time you want to dock it. Regardless, if you have a thick cover (i.e., Otterbox or Reiko) it will not fit on the docking station no matter how much you adjust it. So you must remove the thicker covers (like Otterbox) before you can dock it. My son complained that this was a hassle/extremely inconvenient, especially when he can leave his cover on and simply plug it into the wall. He didn't think that removing the cover to charge outweighed the inconvenience of removing it. However, a slimmer case (less protective ones), like those decorative/fashion ones (i.e., Kate Spade, etc) will fit on the Belkin.

Cost: $82 is very expensive for a product that isn't a must have or at least one that is useful. I am not sure that this product would be a good investment.

Overall, I give the Belkin Power House Dual Charge and Sync Docking station 2.5 out of 5 stars.

Slept two nights with these headphones in their stock configuration and decided I could create something far superior.
For several years I’ve owned and extensively used a pair of the original wired SleepPhones. They are extremely comfortable. The drivers are only 2-3mm thick and sandwiched between two layers of felt. The fleece headband stayed in place without feeling constrictive. It was also easy to wash - open the hook and loop closure on the back, pulled out the speakers and wires, wash, dry, re-install.
By contrast, MusiCozy uses thicker drivers (granted, the frequency response is better than the SleepPhone drivers) then adds a rubber cover, then covers that with a thin jersey fabric. The headband was painfully tight, and I don’t have a big head (22.5”). After the first night, I stretched the headband over a small throw pillow for a day and that helped a bit. But the second night, the thick drivers hurt my ears so bad I took the whole thing off. I mostly sleep on my side and stomach. It’s also tricky to charge because the port is only accessible if you line up the slit in the jersey fabric just right. Some simple product testing would have identified these issues. But for $20, I couldn’t be happier….. why?
SleepPhoness wants $100 for their bluetooth units. I’m sure they are top-notch but I didn’t want to spend that much. Here’s my solutions: The entire MuziCozy headband was disassembled….all two components. The bluetooth receiver / battery compartment and speakers come out easily enough. The fake ‘control panel’ on the front isn’t needed. The speakers have a rubber cover that is not needed. Once that is removed, the speakers are only 3-4mm thick, which is good. I disassembled the wired SleepPhones as well. The felt driver covers were re-used with the MuziCozy drivers, then the whole thing was re-installed into the SleepPhone headband.
This is the best setup - the headband is comfortable, I can still use it to cover my eyes, the sound quality is improved, and the MuziCozy charge port is easier to access thanks to the large velcro opening on the back of the headband.
My girlfriend, by contrast, likes absolute silence while sleeping so she uses the MuziCozy headband to make sure her earplugs don’t fall out and to cover her eyes.
So the entire unit has gone to good use, just not in the way it was delivered. I’m happy with the results but the original product need some redesign.

I don't bang keys loudly or carelessly when I typed, and given that I hadn't had the keyboard for very long, I assumed it the product arrived with a defective key. After a few days, I looked at my F2 key (bluetooth key)- I touched this key maybe ONCE while connecting to my iPhone- and found it LOOSE! I can't snap it back into place because of the same broken plastic issue.

2) Logitech does not have/provide spare keys: When I called Logitech to inquire about spare board keys (rather than returning the entire keyboard to Amazon, because I did really love it besides this key popping problem), the customer service representative offered to replace the entire keyboard, which is great, but he also made mention of the fact they they DID NOT MAKE/PROVIDE spare keys for this model. This means that in the future, if just one key becomes problematic, the customer will have to go through the struggles of shipping out the entire keyboard, etc. I confirmed with the customer service representative that they did IN FACT not make spare keys (I was shocked), but perhaps I had spoken with a particularly new/tired/unversed representative.

All that being said, I am awaiting for a replacement from Amazon (I figured the shipping would be faster w/Amazon's superb customer service), and will see whether the new keyboard presents with problematic keys.
Hope the above two caveats help.

But the biggest issue is the roughness. It’s just too much.

First and worst, the dimensions are not right. It’s 6 x 10, not 7 x 8. Secondly, you get three screen protectors, but only one packet of application materials. Which consists of one wet wipe (which was dry as a bone), one dry wipe,, and a 2 in. microfiber cloth. The wipes were the tiniest ones I’ve ever seen. It was almost impossible to try to clean the screen without touching it with my fingers because the wipes were minuscule. And, like I said, the wet one was dry anyway. I had to supply my own alcohol. And they only supplied wipes for one screen protector. I guess you’re on your own for the other two. One of the protectors was damaged on arrival with a crease in it. This had to happen before shipping because there’s no way to crease one and not the other two. The quality of the screen protector seems very poor. It’s very frosted and seems to inhibit the touch sensitivity of the device. The only positive thing I have to say about it is that it was cheap. But it wasn’t even worth the low price.

This device looks good, and it’s an OK hotspot. But it’s not worth $170, especially when you factor in the incredibly expensive data that is the main selling point. i’m paying 50 bucks per month for 50 GB of prepaid data on T-Mobile. GlocalMe is $36 for 10gb and that’s US only. Usually when a company is trying to entice people to subscribe to expensive recurring service, they do so by providing a cheaper device. In this case, the device is pretty expensive and so is the service. Of course, I knew about all that in advance. What I didn’t know was that the battery life was going to be so poor. I hope they manage to get their data prices down to a more realistic level. They may be good for international travel. I haven’t explored that yet because my T-Mobile and Google Fi has worked well when I’ve traveled overseas so far.

I thought this would be good because they say it has silica gel on the pad. That stuff is super sticky and I knew it would hold my phone quite well because I have a pad of it on my dashboard and my phone doesn’t go anywhere when I put it on that. Unfortunately, it doesn’t have silica gel. It has plain, small, rather cheap plastic suction cups all over the platform.  It’s a shame. It would be a really cool design if it actually was what they say it is.
I love the idea of this, but the screw doesn’t tighten down enough to hold binoculars securely.
The covers are OK but a little flimsy. The mounting brackets are awful. Thin plastic and extremely cheap mounting attachments. I don’t think they’ll last a month.

I upgraded to this when my Netgear unite explore hotspot had a swollen battery, and I decided it was time to upgrade instead of paying for another battery. Unfortunately, it doesn’t really feel like an upgrade. First of all, you need to use an app to access most of the information and settings on the device. I miss being able to change those settings on the display like I could with the Explore. But the big problem is that the Wi-Fi range is not as good. I have an art studio shed that’s about 30 feet from the hotspot. With my old unite explore I had no trouble reaching that shed. With the M1, it’s almost unusable. I like the fact that it includes bands that were not available on my old hotspot, but I don’t like the fact that the range is so much lower.  And I don’t understand why when the device is so huge. That’s another issue. I could put the explorer in my pocket and take it with me, I’m going to need a suitcase for the M1. Edit: after a couple months, I really regret buying this hotspot. It performs so much more poorly than the Explore that it replaced.  And having to do everything through the clunky app which is not built for iPad, is a severe pain. WPS? Forget it. I have a GLI Puli hotspot for my T-Mobile account, and it wiped the floor with this M1 for less than half the price.
I tried to use this to extend my Wi-Fi into my outdoor art studio shed, and it really didn’t make any difference at all that I could tell. If anything, it made it worse.

If you never plan to use the type cover, this may be an OK case for you. I do use the keyboard cover all the time and I found it the case was just too bulky. And it was difficult to remove. I got it because I wanted more protection for the tablet when it was in my backpack or a bag or whatever. But I have taken to just using a regular sleeve that I remove when I’m using it. Once again, if you’re not constantly using the type cover and you only use your surface as a tablet, this is probably a pretty good case.

This is the second time I have tried to use these nano stations. Both times ended in aggravation and returns. Both times I successfully set up the device to receive the Internet, and both times after anywhere from 2 to 12 hours they would lock up and require a reset. Over and over. Once is a bad device. Twice is a bad concept. Enough already. I’m going with the Alfa Camp Pro. Overpriced, but is it overpriced if it actually WORKS? We shall see.

The fake leather frame around the screen is too big. It's difficult to swipe in or top tap. Worst of all, the cutout for the brightness sensor is too small. Since the frame is also fairly thick, it tends to throw a shadow on the sensor. This leads to annoying brightness shifts when you shift positions. The case it pretty but it's just a little too clunky overall.

I bought 6 of these mounts. After less than 2 weeks three of the cameras have come loose and are now hanging upside down and swinging in the breeze and alerting every minute. I’m 4000 mi away so my choices are let the batteries run out, rendering the cameras useless, or disable motion detection, rendering the cameras useless.  I should have stuck with the regular blink mounts. This was an absolute waste of money.

I don’t know if it’s the crappy reader they include or if it’s the cards themselves but I’m encountering frequent errors. Finally a few of them quit working altogether.  And that included card reader....please. I've gotten better stuff out of a crackerjack box. Finally, one of them is only a 2 GB card!!!  What's up with that???
Doesn't fit in the provided bag. I'm also not very impressed with the sound quality.

I guess I’m spoiled by my Wyze Pan cams. The setup for this camera was a pain and if there’s a way to make it track moving objects like my Wyze Pan does, I haven’t figured out how. The hardware of the Dericam seems good, it is amazingly quiet, but the clunky app drags it down.

First of all, I'm using this on windows since my macbook died. I am not overjoyed with the reliability. I copied hundreds of gigabytes of files onto this drive in preparation to move them to a different computer. When I plugged the drive in, it was empty. I've had files go missing off this before but nothing like this. I have no faith in it now.

I tried to love these cameras but they've let me down several times now.  Their motion detection is erratic at the best of times and since there's no ability to continuously record to an sd card or anything else, if the the motion detector doesn't catch it, it's not recorded. It takes too long for the cameras to wake up so I get a lot of 'blank' clips, where whatever finally triggered the camera is over by the time it gets around to recording it. Worst of all, the whole system has a tendency to randomly go offline where it stops communicating with the cameras and nothing gets recorded. After the neighbors annoying free-roaming dogs set off my Wyze cam for the 20th time today it suddenly occurred to me to wonder why I wasn't getting Blink alerts. So I checked, and lo and behold, I wasn't able to connect to any of the cameras, and apparently hadn't been connected for at least 18 hrs based on the last stored clips. But there's no indication of any problem on the aggravatingly bright leds on the hub, they look like everything is peachy. I had to unplug the hub for a few minuted then reconnect. Not so convenient when you're not home, which is when you most definitely want your cameras to work. This is the second time this has happened and I'm done. Returning these.

So I bought another one as I did like the LCD screen. Well, not even a month later Hurricane Michael hit. I had a bunch of sensitive electronics plugged into this and half of them did not survive the power surge when our power went out. My brand new 50" Fire TV, security system DVR and Arlo base unit were all casualties. It did nothing to protect my stuff. My insurance company has a limit on power surge damage and I'm pretty sure this is going to amount to more than that. Do not buy this unit. Utter junk.  I would give it zero stars if I could.

I wrote to customer service and they sent me a link to a YouTube video of a wireless system. :-(  Sadly I let the 30 day window elapse so am stuck with it now.

These units seem to be terribly inconsistent. Setup was a giant pain.  First there were a lot of errors connecting to the server.  Then when I tried to input my lifetime maps code, I got the message that I had to update my software first.  Fine, I'll do that.  Click on the update and get the error that there's not enough space on the device.  Ok, I'd read about this problem.....backed the device up so I could delete all the voices except for one. *UPDATE ON REVIEW AFTER A FEW DAYS OF USE.
After installing the unit and using it for a few days it now has pop up ads on screen and wants you to purchase subscription services for extra features that were not mentioned in the description of the item. The ads make the unit difficult and unsafe to use while driving. We would not recommend this product.

ORGINAL INSTALL REVIEW BEFORE THE POP-UP ADS.
Pros: As the headline says, everything you need to install is included in the box including a backup camera and GPS antenna. The wire harness adapter is pre-wired to plug the unit directly into your factory harness/plugs without splicing any wires. It mounts directly up to the stock radio location without the use of any installation adapters or cutting plastics. The stock plastic trim plate aligns perfectly over the unit once installed and keeps a clean factory look. Optional RCA plug wire harnesses and USB tether plugs are also included for compatibility with your own custom aftermarket external sound equipment if needed. It works with both Apple CarPlay and Android Auto enabled cell phones. It can be used as a mobile Wi-Fi internet hotspot for passengers when paired with your cellphone. System updates can be downloaded directly to the unit through home or cell Wi-Fi once installed. If you have steering wheel controls, they can be manually programed from a menu on the unit to do the functions intended.

Cons: Menus are a little confusing and hard to find "while doing the initial radio setup". The EQ setting screen is hard to find and the HiFi setting (which acts a volume/bass boost) should be turned off if are using stock factory Jeep speakers. HiFi is turned on by default and it makes the volume level far too loud on the stock speakers at its lowest possible volume knob setting. Once the EQ and HiFi 0n/0ff settings are set to your ideal preferences you won’t need to navigate to the EQ screen again. Last minor con is when/how you exit your installed Aps. You’ll need to swipe them completely off the screen to stop them from running in the background and slowing the unit down similar to a cellphone.

Overall: Lots of features. Easy downloadable state maps for NAVI. Easy to download updates. Sounds better than the stock Jeep CD player once the EQ setting have been adjusted. Has a microphone intergraded into the faceplate. Easy to customize the display brightness, colors, wallpaper, and sounds. All the buttons/knobs are backlit with your headlight activation. It will play movies and MP3s.

This camera comes with all the accessories listed. I think the best of them is the light, the mic, the remote, and the two batteries. Battery power is actually pretty good. Picture quality is okay, but the color isn't balanced well, the videos have sort of a grey tone to them. The listing said the item was gold or either had a gold case and that was not the case. These ARLO Q (no base, wired version) cameras get IP addresses from your home network and have their own MAC addresses, and yet, you can't use common software that you can use to view most other IP cameras.

According to their technical support, that's because these IP & MAC address wielding cameras, aren't IP cameras.

You basically don't interact with the cameras, AT ALL. Cameras call their servers, you setup an account on Netgear's servers, and you view what the camera sees Netgear's servers from a website and configure everything on Netgear's website, not the camera's website or interface.

Because of this back and forth ALL "LIVE" VIDEO IS A GOOD 10 SECONDS LAGGING!!!

My roommate, for example, was standing in front of me, before the live feed showed her walking up to the door, getting her keys, and unlocking the door and coming in. And I have 160kbps uploads with Comcast!

What's worse is the motion detection (attached video). Both from front porch or backyard get some leaf shadow at SOME point of the day. And that sets these cameras off constantly. Set at MINIMUM motion detection sensitivity. So I basically can't use them for Motion Detection at ALL since they have dozens of false alarms every single day. Worse yet? At nights, the headlights from every car passing by, sets off the motion detection. AT MINIMUM setting. On both cameras.

A couple of days before I bought these, I also ordered a FOSCAM R4 from Amazon for half the price of one of these cameras. It has tilt, pan, and four times the resolution. You can talk to the camera. You can configure the camera on it's own site. You can interface to it using common IP camera software, OR you can treat them like these, have them call home to their servers, and do everything there. The option is super nice.

Also the FOSCAM's motion detection does not get set off with all the false positives mentioned above.

Their tech support is your generic out of the country, going through unrelated scripts of steps rather than someone knowledgable.

You HAVE to use browser plugins (run full EXEs) or their app. You can NOT access or configure this thing through only a browser (without using their plugin).

The Camera plugin works only in IE, while the MyFoscam.com plugin works only in Edge. It's armature hour, get a wired or wireless Arlo Q, or a Blink. They have their flaws too, but not as bad as this one (I have all three).

FOSCAM forwards you to AmcrestCloud.com for their cloud service. AmcrestCloud will not accept R4 information. Their tech support says they only recommend their own cameras. It keeps thinking my username/password is not the admin one, but it is, and the previous page VERIFIES it, so there is noway to get here if it wasn't (see picture). Their support agrees, they have no clue what's wrong.

You can view the camera (not setup monitoring/alarms ect) on their own site. I tried setting things up through their cloud support, and it wants access to everything, including your admin password on your camera, which in turn has your email username & password (in order to send you emails) and your home network wifi SID and password. Not to mention access to everything the camera is seeing and hearing. And even then it can't fully configure you cam, and the picture it receives for live viewing is horrible (cloud view gets the subset/low res).

Both their viewing, or Amcrest's non-functioning cloud recording/remote-viewing REQUIRE the administrative username and password, despite being able to setup Viewer and Operator accounts. The Admin account of course in turn has access to all your other passwords for email and wifi and such.

It suddenly started having a grainy picture after dusk, and those grains move, so it CONSTANTLY goes off every few seconds. I also tried reducing the detection areas and setting the sensitivity to minimum. This morning I have thousands of email alerts.

Our antenna rotor broke and for 3 years we have been waiting for new chips to come through so we could get another one. It has taken WAY too long. I got this to help with the problem in the meanwhile. What I got was MORE problems.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a blister pack. It has a long cord and a double tail plug on it. The idea is that you put the plug into the antenna spot on the TV and the other is a USB port that you put into your TV. There is a sticker to put this on the wall and instructions.

HOW THIS WORKS
I have had no end of frustration with this thing. We do not have an OLD TV but we do not have any USB ports in this that work with the antenna. The outlets are such that I can not fit ANY adapters into the plug to use an adapter for the USB. The cord from the USB to the intersection where the antenna cord is is very short- only 13 inches. Put that together with the other cord for the antenna which is also about 13 inches and you can not spread them tightly so you only have about 22 to 24 inches tops to get from the TV on the wall down to a USB outlet if you don't have USB on your TV.

I TRIED TO MAKE THIS WORK
I have tried many different USB adapters to get this to work and none of them will work with this unit. I am frustrated and have spent so much time on this, I am giving up. I really wanted this to work, but despite this being an HDTV, it just isn't working out with this unit. I guess we will have to go without antenna TV on that TV longer.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you have USB available on your TV and an antenna hook up, this might work for you. If you don't have a USB port that will work with this unit, you will have to have an available plug that has USB conversion in it, or USB on a power strip that is not more than 24 inches away from the antenna jack on the TV to make it work. You can also use an extension cord and adapter, but honestly, it is a lot of expense for a unit that might or might not work as you like.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. I can not give this a terrible rating like I want to in my frustration. To be fair, three stars is about right. I do not like that it does not come with adapters or alternatives for TVs. Most people who watch antenna TV do not always have the newest equipment. We happen to have this TV that needs the hookup. We have another TV which is newer but the picture is not that great and we already have it set up with another antenna hookup.

I would like this a LOT better if it came with a streamlined USB plug adapter for the power outlets.

UPDATES
If by some miracle, I can find a USB adapter that will fit in this situation and actually WORK, I will update this review and reconsider the rating. For now, it stays as it is. I have put enough time and resources into trying to make this work.

We have had the best time with our antenna. The rotor on top of the roof made it so that we could pick up literally HUNDREDS of stations from the US and Canada. It was delightful. Then the rotor broke. Then Covid wiped out all businesses and we have not been able to get a new rotor since.

HOW THIS WORKS
This antenna is very thin like a piece of paper almost (not quite). You attach it to the TV where you would put the antenna plug in. The app shows you were to put the antenna and you have 18 ft cord to move around to do it. Once up, you set the channels and you are good to go.

HOW THIS REALLY WORKS
For us this was frustrating. The app was meh, but we are pretty limited in our choices of where to put the antenna anyway. We put this antenna in the best place we could find. At first we got lots of channels. Okay, well nowhere near 100, but about 45. It beats the 10 channels we were getting with the broken rotor and the antenna freely spinning in the wind.

The problem comes later. We would sit down to watch a channel we liked, it was gone. I mean GONE. Then we would rescan and were down to only 15 channels. Some of them were in and out. We relocated the antenna and got channels for a while, but then they were gone again.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This will bring in lots of channels, but only at certain times. We have the antenna in almost the same location as our roof antenna (just slightly lower) and we can not pull in channels nearly as well as with the antenna when it is working. Day by day channels we NEVER lose don't come in anymore.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. This brings in some, but not nearly what we are used to. We live in a VERY high hill. there should not be this kind of difficulty in bringing in channels and having them come in consistently. I am referring to channels we get with our spinning antenna on the roof. They don't even come in consistently with this thing. We were hoping this could help until we can get a new rotor.

After several month of irregular channels pulling in and having to struggle, we are putting it back on our spinning roof antenna I think. We don't get quite as many but we at least got the local channels consistently.

I originally wanted this mirror as an inexpensive way to hold makeup classes. I was planning to do in person training as a makeup artist. Having mirrors with lights on them for proper lighting enables me to go wherever I need to go and I don't have to worry about proper lighting as I am bringing it with me. I also wanted to have a mirror with lighting for clients on location if necessary in places without adequate lighting. Let's take a look.

HOW THIS COMES
This light comes folded up in a really ingenious package. It is in a box with the cord attached. There is a clip and a phone holder also that comes with this. Lastly there is a very scant instruction paper.

LIGHT
The light is perfect. It allows me to test out makeup in various lighting to demonstrate how makeup changes based upon where you plan to spend your time that day. The different temperatures and different levels work out quite well for doing a variety of makeup.

MIRROR
The mirror is small, but adequate for doing makeup when teaching tricks and techniques in person. There is a peel off clear protector that will make the mirror look odd so check to see if you forgot that if you think it looks off.

BASE
The base of this is not my favorite. I LOVE that it has places to put my tools and makeup for teaching. This allows me to put what I need for the client in the bins for simple applications so they are not distracted. What I don't like about it is that this mirror is top heavy when fully extended. The base should be a bit heavier and wider.

STEM
This stem extends to a little over two feet. There are 3 stages of extension. The first and second levels are balanced, but the third makes the mirror tip easily. The bottom has to be weighted if you want to use the third level.

PHONE HOLDER
I tried to use this for tutorials and I didn't like the angles. It just did not do what I needed it to do. I was too frustrated with the top heavy tendencies of the full extension and then the lower extension made it harder to record. I prefer other set ups for recording.

AS A MAKEUP MIRROR
This works well as a simple makeup mirror. I also suggest it as a travel makeup mirror, especially if you are an entertainer or need to do makeup on the go. The choices of lighting and the small footprint for packing make it handy to bring with you without taking up too much room.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This mirror is fine for doing in person makeup or personal makeup as I originally got it for. For doing tutorials and recording, I am not fond of the angles, the holder, the top heavy tendencies of the mirror and the lower settings for accuracy in tutorials.

MY RATING
THREE STARS for this over all. I like it for personal and in person making training, but for filming which is what most will want this for, I am not fond of it. The lighting is great, just the design is a bit lacking. For the price, however, it is a decent beginners mirror and light set up.

WHAT IS THIS STEREO LIKE?
First of all, the write up when I had the opportunity to get this stereo said it was a mini stereo system (different than it is now). I expected it to fit where my other stereo system is which was also a condensed system. Boy was I surprised. This system is a LOT bigger than I expected it to be, but still will fit where I wanted to put it although much tighter than I thought it would.

This system has a CD/bluetooth base to it. There is a dial which is rather large on the front that deals with volume. The CD player has the usual controls on it and there is only an FM radio, no AM. There is an infrared remote which has all of the controls you would need to run the stereo.

LIST OF CONNECTORS
FM Antenna terminal
Line 1 and 2 terminals
Speaker light terminal
Speaker out terminal
USB input on front
Headphone jack on front

MEASUREMENTS
Receiver: 11 x 11 13/16 x 5 5/8
Speakers: 12 x 10 3/4 x 16 5/16
Speaker cords approx 2 ft

HOW DOES THIS UNIT PERFORM?
The CD drawer in the bottom right corner operates about average as far as loading and reading. When playing a CD there were not any problems. As far as the equalizer goes, there are only five functions (one is flat- ewww). For this price there should have been more or customizable options.

The equalizer options sound okay, but the two that we choose most often for a variety of music is jazz and rock. Pop, flat, classic seem lack luster for all of the CDs we tried including classical, rock, country, jazz, hip hop, etc.

Despite limitations, the sound did separate well on one of our CDs which has very muffled and quiet background noise at the beginning of a song that we have never heard clearly before.

SOUND QUALITY
The highs come through pretty well, due to the two tweeters per speaker. The mids and lows depend on the music. They tend to suffer more. It booms but not overly clearly. This is more of a mediocre sound that is designed to pump at very high volumes such as for a party. This is not high fidelity sound if that is what you are looking for.

SPEAKER LIGHTS
Although they are interesting at first, the lights seem kind of odd. For the price, it should have had better options. You can choose colors that stay on and do not blink or change out of seven choices. You can choose to have it flash and change color continuously, or you can choose to have the lights flash fast and change continuously, or you can flash the light in white. None of the settings go in time with the music.

You can also opt for no lights on as well. The lights do connect to the speakers by a second wire- it is not in with the speaker connector.

BLUETOOTH
The bluetooth took a while to recognize on the phone. We used android. Once it was paired, many types of music from old to new tracks, and older songs were not as clear or loud as newer tracks. As far as decoding from the bluetooth, it sounded pretty good and did not drop once.

RADIO
The FM sound on this was good and no complaints. Reception was pretty standard, nothing remarkable, but not horrible either.

REMOTE
Remote has to be pointed directly at the receiver. There were a few times where we had to press buttons twice because it would not pick up the signals. The remote itself is black and very small, which makes it easy to misplace. Marking it with neon paint is something we are going to do to make it harder to lose.

PROS
Nice and loud
Picks up highs very well
Bluetooth and CD player in one both work well
Two tweeters per speaker is nice

CONS
Remote very small
Lights sometimes are annoying
Wires are way too short- speakers can not be separated to put in corners of room
Speaker wires are proprietary to the receiver with special attachment (can not use other speakers)

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you want to have a good middle of the road stereo with nice separation of highs and decent sound, you might like this one. The lights and loud capacity also make this a great party unit if you like to fill up a large room or house with sound. Remote works okay , but speakers can not be separated very far. Due to proprietary speaker connections, the only way to change that would be to splice the wires if you are good at electronics.

RATING
This stereo is rather high priced for what you get. It does not have any bass boost, or customizing options for the equalizer. The sound is loud, but not overly high quality. Although this is not a bad unit, it really is not jaw dropping either. I want to give this THREE AND A HALF STARS due to the price and what you get for it. Unfortunately there is only a choice between four and three stars.

Several of my family have been into taking photos for a long time. We have been through quite a few cameras, although not top of the line, still not inexpensive by any means. $500 is usually the price range of cameras we have purchased.

The Fujifilm FinePix S1 is a contradiction of sorts. You might say there is a love-hate relationship with it.

WHAT WE LIKE
Camera lightweight for what is in it
Easy grip- to hang on to and hold
Great neck strap
Macro and Supermacro capabilities are good
Durable
WiFi feature works great with tablet (android OS)
50X zoom works great (have to have very steady hand for that)
Great movies for what it is
Mini HDMI port works for TV or monitor
Photos with flash turn out well consistently
Left and right zoom buttons come in VERY handy
Takes decent self portraits, although a bit clumsy at times to hold
Timer worked well

WHAT WE DON'T LIKE
Navigation can be frustrating
Directional pad can be frustrating
Light sensor is unstable
Automatic settings very unstable and inconsistent
Photos look better on LCD pad than they actually are
Sometimes photos look flat and/or grainy (not 3D looking or clear)

THE BOTTOM LINE

THE LIGHT PROBLEM
We tested this camera extensively inside, outside, at night, in indirect light and with sunlight and found that the light sensor in this camera is way too inconsistent for satisfying picture taking. Sometimes the colors captured were exquisite and better than any other camera I have ever used. I didn't have to do any adjusting at all. Other times they were abyssmal.

For instance, in taking 10 pictures in a row, changing absolutely nothing, it was virtually impossible to have two pictures turn out alike. They were all vastly different. Sometimes they were dark, sometimes way too light, sometimes perfect. That is a lot of effort to capture the perfect picture.

On the flip side, one night in absolute frustration not being able to capture anything decent at all, I turned out all of the lights so that the room was pitch black. I held my camera up to my fish tanks and snapped a few pictures. Besides traumatizing my fish from the sudden light, I was shocked to see some of the most beautiful photos I had taken all evening. Perfect colors, clarity and definition consistently.

It appears that when you use the flash, that the color calibration kicks into high gear and you get pretty darned good photos.

You can not live your life taking flash photos unfortunately.

PHOTO QUALITY
I found that by using various settings and experimenting, I could get pretty nice photos- but I had to use a lot of effort. The menu is not easy to navigate, nor is it forgiving if you take too long to decipher it- it shuts off on you and you have to go through it again.

I did find that sometimes I was taking what I thought were fantastic photos (from the LCD screen) only to upload them to my photo editing program and seeing that they were grainy or blurry or just plain flat and un-dimensional. On the LCD screen they looked amazing. On the other hand, sometimes they turned out blah on my LCD screen, but great on the SD card.

Once in a while, I have problems with my Canon with color. I love bright colors and my photography focus is often color oriented. Canon often understates color way too much for me and I have to spend some time to get it to look accurate in photo editing. With the FinePix S1, however, once in a while, I could capture color that was so gorgeous and realistic that I would gasp and be very excited.

The problem is that it is not always predictable and that was frustrating. Like the proverbial carrot on the string in front of the horse, I find myself reaching for this camera when frustrated with my others to capture colors that don't seem to do well on any other camera. Once in a while the effort is worth it so I come back for more frustration.

FINAL COMMENTS
As I said at the beginning, I have a bit of a love hate relationship with this camera. On the one hand it is a lot of work to get decent photos, but on the other hand, when you do manage to get one, it is amazing. Rare, but amazing.

If Fujifilm would fix the issues with depth in photos, consistency in the light sensor, and quality issues on automatic settings, this camera would be a MUST buy. As it is now, however, I can only give it three stars because of the inconsistency in quality of photos and the effort I have to go through to get a good one. I gave it three stars because once in a while it does capture photos with brilliant colors that none of my other cameras will capture, despite the slightly lower quality at times. The videos are great- sound excellent and clarity nice. The flash is great. Out of the way when you don't want it- and nice photos. It has potential to be a fantastic camera.

As it is now, until they correct a few things, it is only average.

These were much less expensive than the OEM earpads, and you get what  you pay for. They almost work; hard to keep them connected to the headphones. (Maybe I'm not installing them correctly.) They include a plastic pry tool to remove the original worn earpads. These are considerably less comfortable than the original pads, and make the headphones somewhat uncomfortable to wear. Not horrible, just not as good. Someday I might splurge for the OEM pads.

There are some very nice features to these buds, and I do intend to keep them. (Another reviewer was about to return them.) But there are some things that just aren't as good as I had hoped. I'll try to be as detailed as possible.

First, the out-of-box experience is kinda nice, but not fabuous. The smallish box presents the much smaller charger box that the buds live in, and a tiny box that contains a charger cable. Wait -- are there really no instructions? And I thought there were interchangable ear thingies to accommodate ears of different sizes. Ok, so the very brief instruction book clings to the top of the box because it's too big not to fall out on its own. And the ear thingies are hiding in the box where the charging cable is. I seem to be ok with the default ear thingies that are already installed on the buds. (Note, you have to use your own charger with the charging cable. You probably already have too many of those.)

You'll need to download and install the Galaxy Wearable app (on Android, a different one is available for iOS). The app helps you connect to the buds, pretty easy, and is reasonably fully functional. There are numerous options you can play with.

The fit -- quite comfortable actually. Looking at the peculiar shape, I wondered whether these would stay in my ears, and whether they would be uncomfortable. Yes, they stay put, even when walking around, and no, not uncomfortable. This was a pleasant surprise; Samsung really got this part right. I feel as though I could wear these at the office all day and not get ear fatigue. Much, much better than a clumsy pair of headphones slipping off my head when I'm walking around. When wearing the buds, you can hear outside sounds/conversations very well, and perhaps that's the whole idea of these buds. I like this.

There's an equalizer section on the app's main screen. The equalizer options are sort of ok, but not wonderful. I don't know why there's no option for a 10-band graphic equalizer. I just settled on the default after not liking the other choices any better.

You can turn on and off the ANC (active noise cancellation). I have a pair of conventional headphones (not Bose) with ANC that works really well. You feel like you're in a cocoon. These buds have ANC that you can barely tell is working. It sounds a little different, maybe even a little bit of an improvement, but it doesn't seem like it's getting rid of any particular noise. So the ANC is sort of a bust.

Now let's talk about sound quality. As I say, I really wanted to love these little guys. The sound quality is good but not great. Maybe I'm expecting too much. My pair of $250 conventional headphones sound spectacular, and I can listen to music for hours with them. These buds aren't that impressive. The sound quality is ok -- just ok. It's not "bad" in any way at all, but it's not great. I listened to an entire CD that I know well and like. The experience was pleasant, but at the end I really wanted to listen to it on the stereo instead. As I say, maybe I'm expecting too much. The sound quality is probably good enough to listen to at work all day. I had the volume up a little too high, and when my test CD was finished and I took the buds out of my ears, I felt that my ears were ringing a little bit. Next time I'll set the volume lower.

As an interesting aside, I'll compare the sound quality to another wearable that I just got, the Bose Frames (audio sunglasses, a weirdly interesting product). The sound from the Bose Frames is "smooth" in a very wonderful way -- much better than the buds. However, the Bose Frames have absolutely no lower end -- no bass sounds at all. The sounds they do have are great. By contrast, these buds are full range, with pretty good bass. But the sound just isn't smooth.

I didn't try to take a phone call., so I don't know how seamless this works. Considering it's Samsung, and I have a Galaxy S9, I bet this works well enough. I'm not very fussy about sound quality on calls -- I just need to be able to understand what's being said. So "good enough" for me is probably not hard to achieve.

There's a "button" on the buds that you press to skip a track, answer a call, etc. It's not a real button, it's just a touch-sensitive area on the outside of the bud. I haven't been able to get this touch point to work reliably. I don't think there's necessarily anything wrong with the bud, probably just my fat fingers.

Bottom line? I think I'll have a use for these, most likely when I want to listen to my own music without disturbing others, and without the very wonderful but cumbersome conventional earphones. When I'm walking out and about, the smooth sound from the Bose Frames is better. So it's a toss-up with the Galaxy Buds Live. They're good enough, but unfortunately not better than that.

If you have TV Ears, you'll need to keep replacing the tips. These are the official tips, but the price is pretty steep for 10 little pieces of foam. I find the TV Ears product in general unsatisfying (mono sound, not very comfortable to wear), but my mom likes it pretty well.

I've used this touchpad off and on at work over the last few weeks. I really tried to like it, but it just doesn't work well enough for it to be my main pointing device. Here are the things that are issues for me:

* Tracking speed is very different from my mouse, which is a standard Dell mouse. This wouldn't be an issue if the touchpad could replace my mouse, but it really can't. There are some good points:

From the many positive reviews, I had high hopes for this. There are a number of frustrating features with this. It does pick up good strong signals when it's aimed at a station's transmitter.

Good points
- Pretty good reception.
- It has dipoles too, which are good for VHF stations, if the stations are nearby.

Not so good points
- The whole thing is unstable, and keeps falling over. It should be weighted (heavier).
- When it does fall over, which is often, the metal antenna elements can bend easily. They're pretty easy to bend back into shape.
- The coax cable comes out of the bottom of the antenna, and it must be routed through the base. The cable doesn't want to stay put, making the antenna even more likely to tip over.
- The shape is unwieldy. That's a function of the antenna elements, inherent in the design. But it makes it awkward to rotate the antenna to point to different stations.
- When the dipole antennas are extended, the whole thing is very top-heavy. It's *really* easy to tip over.

The signal amplifier comes as a separate unit that you connect inline with the coax cable. I haven't found that it makes much difference in reception. If the station is too weak to pick up, the amplifier isn't likely to magically fix it.

This is a lightweight tripod. That's good in that it's real easy to carry around. That's bad in that it's real easy to tip over, or break. With my camera sitting on top of this, it just doesn't look or feel solid. However, for what you get, it's pretty good. Another reviewer warned of the quick release. It looks good to me, but it's very easy to not get the the latch mechanism all the way fully latched. You have to give it an extra push to get it to fully latch closed. Once you do that, I think it will stay latched. But why worry about the quick release coming loose when the entire tripod is so easy to knock over? Nevertheless, this is a good starter tripod. A pro will want something costing 3 or 4 times this one.
Wears off easily.

I ordered the 'Malektronic Interstellar Premium Wireless Noise Cancelling Over-Ear Headphones' for review and would like to share my thoughts.

So I am no audiophile, but I do love a good quality headphone that is built well and sound good. Sounding good or even great is really subjective depending on personal preference. For the going retail price of these Malektronic Interstellar Premium Wireless Noise Cancelling Over-Ear Headphones, I really expected much more than what I personally find these to be. I'll break my experience and thoughts into a few main points that stood out to me.

Comfort - These are comfortable but they don't fit as snug as I would have liked. I have a small head for a 54yro male, and even on the smallest adjustment setting, they just don't hug my ears like I would have hoped for such an expensive set of headphones.

Noise Cancelling - yea this is a big one for me right hear (see what I did there). I am not at all impressed with the Noise Cancelling in these headphones for the price. I mean it's OK, but I have ANC wireless earbuds that do a much better job for about the same price. There are only two settings. ANC On and ANC Off. For me, It's really hard to tell whether I've turned it on or off. There is no indicator like others I have that would either beep or greet you with some kind of prompt letting you know which mode you are in (there are voice prompts when you turn them on or off so why not anything for ANC modes). In fact the only way I can truly tell that it's on or off, is to pause the song and push the ANC button at which point it's pretty clear. However, and with that said, I do notice that when it's on, the music almost sounds more heavy on the Bass. It's almost like the Bass is supposed to give that "ANC" feel. Remember, I am no audiophile but this is just my observation.

Sound - Now I can say this, and that is that these do sound good until you get close to max volume. At which point they just don't hold up to the volume. Not that they get really loud but if you have the ANC on and you are listening to a heavy Bass song, they tend to bottom out just a tad. It's not bad but again for this price point, I would have expected better. The highs are nice but even better when ANC is off. Mids are there and probably sound good in either mode really. Another thing I noticed is that if you take these off while the music is still playing at full volume, they sound like they are rattling and sound a bit distorted. However when you put them back on, there is no distortion like I noticed with them off. That was kind of strange.

Micro USB charging - I always have to point this out. It's 2020 companies and USB C should be the standard any more in my opinion. Just saying.

Build Quality - They aren't the worst I have seen or tried but at this price point they are not the best either. They are pretty much plastic although fairly solid.

Buttons - The buttons are hidden/covered near the edge of the ear pads and they took me a while to figure out where they are, but after using them for a while, I actually like the fact that they look to be buttonless.

Looks/design - These really do look nice both on and off. They don't look cheap which is nice, as I have some others that just look ugly and I refuse to wear haha. The design is well thought out and I do love how they fold flat and compact into the very nice hard case.

So with all that said, I do like these headphones. They sound pretty good. The ANC is meh but they are comfortable besides not fitting as snug as I would prefer. Build quality is decent and I do love they way they fold up and store nicely into the included hard case. Thank you for including this Maletronics! Micro USB charging is a bummer but they also can be used wired with the included cable if you forget to get them charged up. Battery life is not bad. 30hrs might be pushing it if you like to listen to them loud and are always using the ANC. I have yet to test that fully as the longest I generally go is maybe an hour at a time. So for me the battery life is fine.

Overall, I really want to love these, and I actually do like them a lot, but I am just not that "Wowed" at this price point. I have other brands at or around this price point that I like better. Now maybe I got a dud pair and that very well could be, but I don't dislike them. They are nice and I plan to keep them around as a back-up pair. I hope that this was helpful.

I ordered the 'Geeni, Sentry Floodlight Security Camera with Motion Sensor, Intruder Alarm and Audio Video Recording' for review and would like to share my thoughts.

So I have had this camera for a while now and finally got it installed a couple of weeks ago and I am ready to share my thoughts and experience so far. This camera requires hard wiring which is why it took so long to get it installed. In my old home it was going to require me to get an extension cord, drill through my wall in the garage and plug it in, in the garage. This was much more work than I had anticipated. Now the new home already had normal motion sensor lights installed on switches, which made this more feasible for me to install. I took one of the motion sensor lights down and had to retrofit a new mount out of a piece of wood to cover the original hole left by removing the old light. This wasn't to hard to do and the Geeni light mounted with ease. Once installed and I turned the light switch on, it was ready to set up which took some time to do. I had to reset the device several times to get the App to set it up properly which was a quite pain however.

The camera itself is very good but so far I am not happy with all the notifications that I get which seem to be false alerts. It seems that everything seems to trigger this thing with absolutely no control as to how sensitive you would like the sensor to be. This is truly my main con with this device. I ended up turning notifications off on my mobile device which kind of defeats the purpose really.

Then there is the App which has thus far been pretty buggy. It has crashed many times and it is not so easy to find the "actual" activity that it seems to detect. Of all the motion activity that it detects, I would say that only 40% of it is relative. I do have the App set to just record everything (continuous) on the 128gb SD card which makes more sense seeing as there are so many false readings.

As for the good of this Geeni device, the image quality both during daytime and nighttime recording and playback is great. There is very little lag when accessing the footage which is surprising as I have other WiFi cameras that are painfully slow to connect and playback footage. This is probably my favorite feature (when the App doesn't crash).

I am reviewing the ‘TruSound TruWireless Noise Cancelling Earbuds | True Wireless Earbuds with Charging Case for Buds and Phone | Comfortable, Secure Fit | Immersive Stereo Sound, Deep Bass | Easy Touch Control Operation’.
Based on my experience thus far I would like to share my thoughts.

Pros:
1- The sound is decent but compared to other Wireless Earbuds that I have tried, these are pretty average.
2- The case is rechargeable via the included 18650 battery. This allows you to have extra 18650 batteries on hand which is an interesting feature.
3- It comes with extra ear tips.
4- It comes with a mini USB cable and even a USB type A to Mini USB adapter.
5- Aesthetically the earbuds look nice, feel comfortable and don’t protrude much when wearing them.
6- They stay in place quite well and do not randomly fall out.
7- Earbuds are held in place magnetically when in the case charging.
8- They pair up real fast and very easy. I have had no issues at all with pairing.

Cons:
1- I ordered these based on the description stating “active noise reduction is also a standout feature of TruSound ear buds, ensuring a distraction-free audio experience”. I took this as they had ANC or Active Noise Control. This is not the case. These “isolate” the outside sounds via the ear tip inserted into the ear canal. If you get the right tip fit, they do “isolate” the outside sounds but just not as expected.
2- No USB type C. In my opinion all new devices should have USB C charging.
3- The case is a bit bulky due to the fact that it uses the 18650 battery.
4- The case is plastic and uses two plastic tabs to snap the lid closed. The design makes it really hard to open the case once it’s snapped shut. I am worried that I will break the plastic tabs at which point I would need to use a rubber band to keep the lid closed.
5- The Stand-By time is not the greatest. I fully charged the 18650 battery with my own charger when I first got the Earbuds. I used the Earbuds briefly while initially testing them and when I went back a couple of weeks later to try them again, the battery was already dead. I have other earbuds that have this same issue. I should be able to fully charge my earbuds, keep them in my backpack for a few weeks and have them ready to go when I want to use them.
6- No IPX rating? Pretty much all of the newer Earbuds these days have some kind of waterproof rating. It’s not advertised so I am not really sure if they are.
7- No Bluetooth 5.0? These have Bluetooth 4.2+EDR which isn’t bad, but there are sync issues when watching YouTube, Netflix ect. It’s not bad, but it’s noticeable and I could not use these to watch videos for too long.

Overall these TruSound Earbuds are average, and I feel that compared to the flooded market of True Wireless Earbuds these are a bit overpriced. With that said, I do like these but, I do feel there could be some improvements made that would ultimately increase the value.
